title.zh: 卷二百六十五 列傳第一百五十三 范景文 倪元璐 李邦華 王家彥 孟兆祥 施邦曜 淩義渠
title.en: Volume 265 Biographies 153: Fan Jingwen, Ni Yuanlu, Li Banghua, Wang Jiayan, Meng Zhaoxiang, Shi Bangyao, Ling Yiqu
title.raw: 卷二百六十五 列傳第一百五十三 范景文 倪元璐 李邦華 王家彥 孟兆祥 施邦曜 淩義渠 Volume 265 Biographies 153: Fan Jingwen, Ni Yuanlu, Li Banghua, Wang Jiayan, Meng Zhaoxiang, Shi Bangyao, Ling Yiqu

sentences.zh: 範景文倪元璐李邦華王家彥孟兆祥

translations.literal: Fan Jingwen, Ni Yuanlu, Li Banghua, Wang Jiayan, Meng Zhaoxiang
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jingwen, Ni Yuanlu, Li Banghua, Wang Jiayan, and Meng Zhaoxiang

sentences.zh: 〈（子章明）〉

translations.literal: (Zhang Ming, his son)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Zhang Ming, his son)〉

sentences.zh: 施邦曜淩義渠

translations.literal: Shi Bangyao, Ling Yiqu
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bangyao and Ling Yiqu are also treated here.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十有七年三月，流賊李自成犯京師。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, the bandit Li Zicheng attacked the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventeenth year of the Chongzhen reign, the rebel Li Zicheng assaulted the capital.

sentences.zh: 十九日丁未，莊烈帝殉社稷。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day, the day dingwei, Emperor Zhuanglie died for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day, a dingwei day, the Chongzhen Emperor perished with his dynasty.

sentences.zh: 文臣死國者，東閣大學士範景文而下，凡二十有一人。

translations.literal: Among civil officials who died for the state, from Grand Secretary Fan Jingwen of the Eastern Pavilion downward, there were twenty-one in all.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one civil officials died for the dynasty, beginning with Grand Secretary Fan Jingwen of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 福王立南京，並予贈謚。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu established his court at Nanjing, posthumous titles were granted to them all.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Fu raised his standard at Nanjing, they were all granted posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 皇清順治九年，世祖章皇帝表章前代忠臣，所司以範景文、倪元璐、李邦華、王家彥、孟兆祥、子章明、施邦曜、淩義渠、吳麟征、周鳳翔、馬世奇、劉理順、汪偉、吳甘來、王章、陳良謨、申佳允、許直、成德、金鉉二十人名上。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi of the Great Qing, the Shizu Zhang Emperor honored loyal ministers of former dynasties; the responsible office submitted the names of twenty men: Fan Jingwen, Ni Yuanlu, Li Banghua, Wang Jiayan, Meng Zhaoxiang, Zhang Ming, Shi Bangyao, Ling Yiqu, Wu Linzheng, Zhou Fengxiang, Ma Shiqi, Liu Lishun, Wang Wei, Wu Ganlai, Wang Zhang, Chen Liangmo, Shen Jiayun, Xu Zhi, Cheng De, and Jin Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shunzhi, the Shunzhi Emperor commended loyal ministers of earlier dynasties, and the responsible office submitted twenty names: Fan Jingwen, Ni Yuanlu, Li Banghua, Wang Jiayan, Meng Zhaoxiang, Zhang Ming, Shi Bangyao, Ling Yiqu, Wu Linzheng, Zhou Fengxiang, Ma Shiqi, Liu Lishun, Wang Wei, Wu Ganlai, Wang Zhang, Chen Liangmo, Shen Jiayun, Xu Zhi, Cheng De, and Jin Xuan.

sentences.zh: 命所在有司各給地七十畝，建祠致祭，且予美謚焉。

translations.literal: He ordered the local authorities in each place to grant seventy mu of land, build shrines for sacrifice, and bestow fine posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered local officials everywhere to allot seventy mu of land, erect shrines for sacrifice, and grant them honored posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 範景文，字夢章，吳橋人。

translations.literal: Fan Jingwen, style name Mengzhang, was a native of Wuqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jingwen, whose style was Mengzhang, came from Wuqiao.

sentences.zh: 父永年，南寧知府。

translations.literal: His father Yongnian was prefect of Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yongnian had served as prefect of Nanning.

sentences.zh: 景文幼負器識，登萬歷四十一年進士，授東昌推官。

translations.literal: Jingwen showed talent and insight from youth; he passed the jinshi examination in the forty-first year of Wanli and was appointed investigating censor of Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jingwen showed promise and ability. He took his jinshi degree in the forty-first year of Wanli and was appointed investigating censor of Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 以名節自勵，苞苴無敢及其門。

translations.literal: He urged himself on by reputation and integrity; no bribes dared reach his door.
translations.idiomatic: He held himself to the highest standards of integrity, and no one dared offer him a bribe.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，盡心振救，闔郡賴之。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine he devoted himself to relief, and the whole prefecture relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the region, he threw himself into relief work, and the entire prefecture owed him its survival.

sentences.zh: 用治行高等，擢吏部稽勛主事，歷文選員外郎，署選事。

translations.literal: Because his administrative record was rated superior, he was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's merit-records section, served as vice director in the civil appointments bureau, and acted in charge of selections.
translations.idiomatic: Rated highly for his administrative record, he was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's merit-records section, rose through the civil appointments bureau to vice director, and handled selections in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 泰昌時，群賢登進，景文力為多，尋乞假去。

translations.literal: In the Taichang reign many worthy men were advanced; Jingwen had a large hand in it, but soon requested leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: During the brief Taichang reign he helped advance many worthy men, then soon took leave and left office.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年二月，起文選郎中，魏忠賢暨魏廣微中外用事，景文同鄉，不一詣其門，亦不附東林，孤立行意而已。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Tianqi he was recalled as director in the civil appointments bureau. Wei Zhongxian and Wei Guangwei held power inside and outside the court; Jingwen was their fellow townsman yet never once called at their doors, nor did he attach himself to the Donglin faction—he simply stood alone and acted on his own principles.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year of Tianqi he was recalled as director in the civil appointments bureau. Wei Zhongxian and Wei Guangwei dominated court and capital alike. Though a fellow townsman of theirs, Jingwen never called at their doors and refused to join the Donglin faction, standing apart and following his own conscience.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「天地人才，當為天地惜之。

translations.literal: He once said: "The talents of heaven and earth should be cherished for heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "The talents heaven and earth provide ought to be cherished as heaven and earth's own treasure.

sentences.zh: 朝廷名器，當為朝廷守之。

translations.literal: The honored offices of the court should be guarded for the court.
translations.idiomatic: The honored offices of the court ought to be guarded for the court's sake.

sentences.zh: 天下萬世是非公論，當與天下萬世共之。」

translations.literal: The public judgment of right and wrong for all under heaven through ten thousand ages should be shared with all under heaven through ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: The public judgment of right and wrong, for all the world and for all time, should be shared with all the world and for all time.

sentences.zh: 時以為名言。

translations.literal: At the time these words were regarded as famous sayings.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries took these words for maxims.

sentences.zh: 視事未彌月，謝病去。

translations.literal: He had not yet completed a full month in office when he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had served a full month he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，用薦召為太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was summoned on recommendation to be vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he was summoned on recommendation to serve as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，擢右僉都御史，巡撫河南。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 京師戒嚴，率所部八千人勤王，餉皆自賫。

translations.literal: When the capital was placed under martial law, he led eight thousand men of his command to relieve the throne, and all provisions were carried at his own expense.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital went on alert, he led eight thousand troops to its relief and paid for their provisions out of his own purse.

sentences.zh: 抵涿州，四方援兵多剽掠，獨河南軍無所犯。

translations.literal: On reaching Zhuozhou, relief armies from all quarters mostly plundered, but the Henan army alone committed no offenses.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuozhou he found relief armies from every direction looting the countryside, but his Henan troops alone committed no depredations.

sentences.zh: 移駐都門，再移昌平，遠近恃以無恐。

translations.literal: He shifted his encampment to the capital gates, then again to Changping; near and far relied on him and were unafraid.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his camp to the capital gates and then to Changping, and people near and far took heart from his presence.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，擢兵部添註左侍郎，練兵通州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year he was promoted to supplementary left vice minister of war and drilled troops at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following March he was promoted to supplementary left vice minister of war and took charge of training troops at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 通鎮初設，兵皆召募，景文綜理有法，軍特精。

translations.literal: The Tongzhou garrison had just been established and all the troops were recruits; Jingwen managed them with method, and the army became exceptionally sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongzhou garrison was newly established and its soldiers were all recruits, but Jingwen organized them so effectively that the force became exceptionally disciplined.

sentences.zh: 嘗請有司實行一條鞭法，徭役歸之官，民稍助其費，供應平買，不立官價名。

translations.literal: He once asked the local authorities to put the single-whip method into real practice: corvée labor would revert to official management, the people would contribute only a modest fee, supplies would be purchased at fair market rates, and no official price names would be set.
translations.idiomatic: He urged local authorities to implement the single-whip tax reform in earnest: corvée duties would be handled by officials, the people would pay a modest levy, supplies would be bought at fair market rates, and no arbitrary official prices would be imposed.

sentences.zh: 帝令永著為例。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered this to be established permanently as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the practice made a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 居二年，以父喪去官。

translations.literal: After two years in office he left his post on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，起南京右都御史。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year he was recalled as right censor-in-chief at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year he was recalled to serve as right censor-in-chief at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，就拜兵部尚書，參贊機務。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed minister of war on the spot and assisted in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed minister of war and joined in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 屢遣兵戍池河、浦口，援廬州，扼滁陽，有警輒發，節制精明。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent troops to garrison Chihe and Pukou, relieve Luzhou, and block Chuyang; whenever there was an alarm he dispatched forces at once, and his control was keen and precise.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sent troops to garrison Chihe and Pukou, relieve Luzhou, and hold Chuyang. At every alarm he moved swiftly, and his command was sharp and sure.

sentences.zh: 嘗與南京戶部尚書錢春以軍食相訐奏，坐鐫秩視事。

translations.literal: He once exchanged impeachments with Qian Chun, minister of revenue at Nanjing, over military provisions, and was demoted in rank but continued in office.
translations.idiomatic: He once clashed with Qian Chun, the Nanjing minister of revenue, over military rations, exchanging impeachments that cost him a demotion though he remained in office.

sentences.zh: 已，敘援剿功，復故秩。

translations.literal: Later, his merits in relief and suppression were recorded and his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later his merits in relief and suppression were recognized and his former rank restored.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，京師戒嚴，遣兵入衛。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year the capital was placed under martial law, and he sent troops to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year, when the capital went on alert, he sent troops to its defense.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌奪情輔政，廷臣力爭多被謫，景文倡同列合詞論救。

translations.literal: When Yang Sichang left mourning to assist in government, many court officials who argued forcefully were banished; Jingwen led his colleagues in a joint memorial to plead for them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Sichang left mourning to take up office, many officials who protested were exiled. Jingwen led his colleagues in a joint memorial pleading for them.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，詰首謀，則自引罪，且以眾論僉同為言。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and demanded who had led the plot; Jingwen then took the blame on himself and said the opinion of the multitude was unanimous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and demanded to know who had led the effort. Jingwen took the blame on himself and said the court had spoken with one voice.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，削籍為民。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier and struck him from the registers, reducing him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger deepened, and Jingwen was struck from the rolls and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 十五年秋，用薦召拜刑部尚書，未上，改工部。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifteenth year he was summoned on recommendation and appointed minister of justice; before he took up the post he was transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifteenth year he was summoned on recommendation and appointed minister of justice, but before he could take up the post he was transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 入對，帝迎勞曰：「不見卿久，何臒也！」

translations.literal: On entering audience the emperor greeted him with words of comfort, saying: "It has been long since I have seen you—how thin you have grown!"
translations.idiomatic: When he came before the throne, the emperor greeted him warmly: "I have not seen you in so long—how thin you have become!"

sentences.zh: 景文謝。

translations.literal: Jingwen thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen expressed his gratitude.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月，命以本官兼東閣大學士，入參機務。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year he was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion in his present office and enter into deliberations on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year he was appointed concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and admitted to deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李自成破宣府，烽火逼京師。

translations.literal: Before long Li Zicheng captured Xuanfu, and beacon fires pressed upon the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Zicheng took Xuanfu, and warning fires drew near the capital.

sentences.zh: 有請帝南幸者，命集議閣中。

translations.literal: Some urged the emperor to tour south, and he ordered deliberation assembled in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged the emperor to flee south, he ordered the Grand Secretariat to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 景文曰：「固結人心，堅守待援而已，此外非臣所知。」

translations.literal: Jingwen said: "Only to bind hearts firmly together, hold fast and await relief—that is all; beyond this your servant knows nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen said, "We must rally the people's loyalty, hold the city, and wait for relief—that is all I know to advise."

sentences.zh: 及都城陷，趨至宮門，宮人曰：「駕出矣。」

translations.literal: When the capital fell he hurried to the palace gate; a palace attendant said: "The imperial carriage has already departed."
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he rushed to the palace gate. A palace attendant told him, "His Majesty has already left."

sentences.zh: 復趨朝房，賊已塞道。

translations.literal: He hurried again toward the court offices, but the rebels had already blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: He turned toward the court offices, but rebels already blocked the way.

sentences.zh: 從者請易服還邸，景文曰：「駕出安歸？」

translations.literal: His attendants asked him to change clothes and return to his residence; Jingwen said: "The carriage has gone out—where can it return?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants urged him to change clothes and return home. Jingwen said, "If the emperor has left the palace, where can he possibly go?"

sentences.zh: 就道旁廟草遺疏，復大書曰：「身為大臣，不能滅賊雪恥，死有余恨。」

translations.literal: At a roadside shrine he drafted a final memorial, and wrote large characters as well: "As a great minister I could not destroy the bandits and wipe away disgrace; in death I still have more than enough regret."
translations.idiomatic: At a roadside shrine he drafted a final memorial and wrote in large characters: "As a great minister I could not destroy the rebels and avenge this shame. Even in death my regret is more than I can bear."

sentences.zh: 遂至演象所拜辭闕墓，赴雙塔寺旁古井死。

translations.literal: He then went to the Observatory to bow in farewell before the tomb by the palace gate, and threw himself into an old well beside Shuangta Temple to die.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the Observatory to take leave before the imperial tomb, then drowned himself in an old well beside Shuangta Temple.

sentences.zh: 景文死時，猶謂帝南幸也。

translations.literal: At the time of Jingwen's death he still believed the emperor had toured south.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingwen died he still believed the emperor had fled south.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚文貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wen Zhen, "Literary and Upright."

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚文忠。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous title Wen Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty granted him the posthumous title Wen Zhong, "Literary and Loyal."

sentences.zh: 倪元璐，字玉汝，上虞人。

translations.literal: Ni Yuanlu, style name Yuru, was a native of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Yuanlu, whose style was Yuru, came from Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 父凍，歷知撫州、淮安、荊州、瓊州四府，有當官稱。

translations.literal: His father Dong had served as prefect of four prefectures—Fuzhou, Huai'an, Jingzhou, and Qiongzhou—and had the reputation of a worthy official.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dong had governed four prefectures—Fuzhou, Huai'an, Jingzhou, and Qiongzhou—and earned a reputation as a capable official.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，元璐成進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi Yuanlu passed the jinshi examination, was transferred to the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi, Yuanlu passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 冊封德府，移疾歸。

translations.literal: When the Prince of De was invested he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After taking part in the investiture of the Prince of De, he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 還朝，出典江西鄉試。

translations.literal: On returning to court he went out to preside over the provincial examination of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court he was sent to administer the Jiangxi provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 暨復命，則莊烈帝踐阼，魏忠賢已伏誅矣。

translations.literal: When he reported back on his mission, Emperor Zhuanglie had already ascended the throne and Wei Zhongxian had already been executed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reported back, the Chongzhen Emperor had already ascended the throne and Wei Zhongxian had already been put to death.

sentences.zh: 楊維垣者，逆奄遺孽也，至是上疏並詆東林、崔、魏。

translations.literal: Yang Weiyuan was a surviving remnant of the treacherous eunuch faction; at this time he submitted a memorial slandering together the Donglin faction, Cui, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weiyuan was a holdover from the eunuch faction. He now submitted a memorial denouncing the Donglin faction together with Cui and Wei.

sentences.zh: 元璐不能平，崇禎元年正月上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yuanlu could not contain himself, and in the first month of the first year of Chongzhen submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlu could not abide this. In the first month of the first year of Chongzhen he submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣頃閱章奏，見攻崔、魏者必與東林並稱邪黨。

translations.literal: Your servant has recently reviewed memorials and seen that those who attack Cui and Wei are invariably classed together with the Donglin as an evil faction.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has lately reviewed memorials and found that anyone who attacks Cui and Wei is invariably lumped together with the Donglin as members of an evil faction.

sentences.zh: 夫以東林為邪黨，將以何者名崔、魏？

translations.literal: If the Donglin are called an evil faction, by what name then shall Cui and Wei be known?
translations.idiomatic: If the Donglin are an evil faction, what name then shall we give Cui and Wei?

sentences.zh: 崔、魏既邪黨矣，擊忠賢、呈秀者又邪黨乎哉！

translations.literal: If Cui and Wei are already an evil faction, are those who struck at Zhongxian and Chengxian also an evil faction!
translations.idiomatic: If Cui and Wei were the evil faction, then were those who struck down Zhongxian and Chengxian also an evil faction?

sentences.zh: 東林，天下才藪也，而或樹高明之幟，繩人過刻，持論太深，謂之非中行則可，謂之非狂狷不可。

translations.literal: The Donglin are a gathering place for the talents of the empire; some among them may raise banners of lofty rectitude, bind others too strictly, and hold their arguments too deep—one may call this not the middle way, but one cannot call it other than the fierce and upright.
translations.idiomatic: The Donglin were a gathering place for the empire's best minds. Some among them may have held themselves too loftily, judged others too harshly, or argued too fiercely—one may call that falling short of the middle way, but not falling short of passionate integrity.

sentences.zh: 且天下議論，寧假借，必不可失名義；

translations.literal: Moreover, in the discourse of the empire one may tolerate pretense, but one must never lose hold of right names and moral principle;
translations.idiomatic: In public discourse one may tolerate a degree of pretense, but one must never abandon right names and moral principle;

sentences.zh: 士人行己，寧矯激，必不可忘廉隅。

translations.literal: in the conduct of gentlemen one may tolerate excess, but one must never forget integrity.
translations.idiomatic: and in a gentleman's conduct one may tolerate excess, but one must never forget integrity.

sentences.zh: 自以假借矯激為大咎，於是彪虎之徒公然背畔名義，決裂廉隅。

translations.literal: Once pretense and excess were taken as great faults, then men like Biao and Hu openly turned their backs on right names and moral principle and ruptured integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Once pretense and excess were treated as the gravest faults, men like Wei Zhongxian's henchmen openly abandoned moral principle and cast integrity aside.

sentences.zh: 頌德不已，必將勸進；

translations.literal: Praise without end must lead to urging the ruler to advance;
translations.idiomatic: Endless flattery must lead to urging the ruler to usurp the throne;

sentences.zh: 建祠不已，必且呼嵩。

translations.literal: shrine-building without end must lead to crying out as Yan Song was cried out to.
translations.idiomatic: endless shrine-building must lead to addressing a minister as though he were the emperor, as Yan Song was addressed.

sentences.zh: 而人猶且寬之曰：「無可奈何，不得不然耳。」

translations.literal: Yet people still indulged them, saying: "There was nothing to be done—they could not have acted otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: Yet people still excused them, saying, "There was nothing to be done—they had no choice."

sentences.zh: 充此無可奈何、不得不然之心，又將何所不至哉！

translations.literal: Fill this heart of "nothing to be done" and "could not have acted otherwise," and what will not be reached!
translations.idiomatic: Indulge that spirit of helpless necessity, and what limit will there be to what men will do?

sentences.zh: 乃議者以忠厚之心曲原此輩，而獨持已甚之論苛責吾徒，所謂舛也。

translations.literal: Yet those who debated bent their generous hearts to excuse these men, while applying harsh standards only to our party—this is what is called perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Yet debaters bent their generous hearts to excuse such men while applying the harshest standards only to our party—that is perversity indeed.

sentences.zh: 今大獄之後，湯火僅存，屢奉明綸，俾之酌用，而當事者猶以道學封疆，持為鐵案，毋亦深防其報復乎？

translations.literal: Now after the great prosecutions only a few survive as if scalded or burned; the court has repeatedly issued clear edicts ordering measured employment, yet those in charge still treat the frontier of Neo-Confucian learning as an iron verdict—is this not deep fear of their revenge?
translations.idiomatic: After the great prosecutions only a handful survive, scorched as if by fire. The throne has repeatedly ordered that they be employed with discretion, yet those in power still treat the Donglin as beyond the pale—is this not fear of their revenge?

sentences.zh: 然臣以為過矣。

translations.literal: Yet your servant thinks this goes too far.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes this goes too far.

sentences.zh: 年來借東林媚崔、魏者，其人自敗，何待東林報復？

translations.literal: In recent years those who used the Donglin to flatter Cui and Wei brought ruin on themselves—why wait for Donglin revenge?
translations.idiomatic: In recent years those who used the Donglin name to flatter Cui and Wei destroyed themselves without any need for Donglin revenge.

sentences.zh: 若不附崔、魏，又能攻去之，其人已喬嶽矣，雖百東林烏能報復哉？

translations.literal: If one did not attach to Cui and Wei and could moreover drive them away, that man already stood like a lofty peak—how could a hundred Donglin factions take revenge?
translations.idiomatic: If a man refused to serve Cui and Wei and helped drive them from power, he already stood like a mountain—what could a hundred Donglin factions do to harm him?

sentences.zh: 臣又伏讀聖旨，有「韓爌清忠有執，朕所鑒知」之諭。

translations.literal: Your servant has again read reverently the imperial edict with the instruction: "Han Kuang is pure, loyal, and principled; We have observed and know this."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also read with reverence the imperial edict stating, "Han Kuang is pure, loyal, and principled; We have observed this and know it to be true."

sentences.zh: 而近聞廷臣之議，殊有異同，可為大怪。

translations.literal: Yet your servant has lately heard the discussions of court officials, which differ greatly—this is truly strange.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your servant has lately heard court opinion sharply divided on the matter—a thing most strange.

sentences.zh: 爌相業光偉，他不具論，即如紅丸議起，舉國沸然，爌獨侃侃條揭，明其不然。

translations.literal: Kuang's ministerial achievement was glorious and great; on other matters I shall not speak in detail. Take for example the Red Pill affair: when it arose the whole realm seethed, yet Kuang alone calmly set forth item by item and showed that it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang's ministerial record was illustrious; I need not rehearse it all. When the Red Pill controversy erupted and the whole realm seethed, Kuang alone calmly laid out the facts and showed the charges were false.

sentences.zh: 夫孫慎行，君子也，爌且不附，況他人乎！

translations.literal: Sun Shenxing was a gentleman, and Kuang would not even attach to him—how much less to others!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shenxing was a man of integrity, and even him Kuang would not court—how much less would he court lesser men!

sentences.zh: 而今推轂不及，點灼橫加，則徒以其票擬熊廷弼一事耳。

translations.literal: Yet now he is not advanced to high office and calumny is heaped upon him—this is solely on account of his memorial recommending Xiong Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now he is passed over for promotion while slander rains down on him—solely because of his memorial recommending Xiong Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 廷弼固當誅，爌不為無說，封疆失事，累累有徒，乃欲獨殺一廷弼，豈平論哉？

translations.literal: Tingbi indeed deserved execution, and Kuang was not without grounds in his view; border failures had offenders in great numbers—yet to wish to kill Tingbi alone, is this fair judgment?
translations.idiomatic: Tingbi deserved punishment, and Kuang was not without grounds in recommending him. Border failures had countless culprits—yet to demand Tingbi's death alone, is that fair judgment?

sentences.zh: 此爌所以閣筆也。

translations.literal: This is why Kuang laid down his brush.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Kuang laid down his brush and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 然廷弼究不死於封疆而死於局面，不死於法吏而死於奸珰，則又不可謂後之人能殺廷弼，而爌獨不能殺之也。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Tingbi did not die on the frontier but died in the political struggle; he did not die at the hands of legal officials but at the hands of treacherous eunuchs—so one cannot say that later men could kill Tingbi while Kuang alone could not.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end Tingbi did not die for frontier failures but for political intrigue; he did not die at the hands of the law but at the hands of treacherous eunuchs. One cannot say that later men had the power to kill Tingbi while Kuang alone did not.

sentences.zh: 又如詞臣文震孟正學勁骨，有古大臣之品，三月居官，昌言獲罪，人以方之羅倫、舒芬。

translations.literal: Again, the academician Wen Zhenmeng had upright learning and firm backbone, the quality of great ministers of old; in three months in office his outspoken words brought punishment, and men compared him to Luo Lun and Shu Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Consider also the academician Wen Zhenmeng, a man of upright learning and firm backbone with the quality of great ministers of old. In three months in office his outspoken words brought punishment, and men compared him to Luo Lun and Shu Fen.

sentences.zh: 而今起用之旨再下，謬悠之譚不已，將毋門戶二字不可重提耶？

translations.literal: Yet now orders for his recall have been issued twice, while absurd and idle talk continues without end—are the two words "factional gate" not to be raised again?
translations.idiomatic: Yet orders for his recall have been issued twice while absurd objections continue—is the word "faction" never to be spoken again?

sentences.zh: 用更端以相遮抑耶？

translations.literal: Are other pretexts to be used to obstruct and suppress him?
translations.idiomatic: Are other pretexts to be found to block his appointment?

sentences.zh: 書院、生祠，相勝負者也，生祠毀，書院豈不當修復！

translations.literal: Academies and living shrines were opposed to each other in victory and defeat; if living shrines are destroyed, should academies not be restored!
translations.idiomatic: Academies and living shrines stood in opposition to each other. If the living shrines are torn down, should not the academies be restored?

sentences.zh: 時柄國者悉忠賢遺黨，疏入，以論奏不當責之。

translations.literal: Those who held power at the time were all surviving followers of Zhongxian; when the memorial entered, he was rebuked on the grounds that his argument was improper.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power were all holdovers from Zhongxian's faction. When the memorial arrived, Yuanlu was rebuked for improper argument.

sentences.zh: 於是維垣復疏駁元璐。

translations.literal: Thereupon Weiyuan submitted another memorial refuting Yuanlu.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan then submitted another memorial refuting Yuanlu.

sentences.zh: 元璐再疏曰：

translations.literal: Yuanlu submitted a second memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlu submitted a second memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣前疏原為維垣發也。

translations.literal: Your servant's previous memorial was originally directed at Weiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's previous memorial was directed at Weiyuan.

sentences.zh: 陛下明旨曰：「分別門戶，已非治征」，曰「化異為同」，曰「天下為公」，而維垣則倡為孫黨、趙黨、熊黨、鄒黨之說。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's clear edict says: "Distinguishing factional gates is already not the sign of good government," says "transform the different into the same," says "all under heaven is public"—yet Weiyuan advocates theories of the Sun faction, the Zhao faction, the Xiong faction, and the Zou faction.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's clear edict declares that distinguishing factions is no sign of good government, that differences should be transformed into unity, and that all under heaven belongs to the public—yet Weiyuan promotes talk of the Sun faction, the Zhao faction, the Xiong faction, and the Zou faction.

sentences.zh: 是陛下於方隅無不化，而維垣實未化；

translations.literal: Thus Your Majesty leaves no corner un-transformed, yet Weiyuan in truth is not transformed;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty leaves no corner of the court un-transformed, yet Weiyuan remains untransformed;

sentences.zh: 陛下於正氣無不伸，而維垣不肯伸。

translations.literal: Your Majesty leaves no upright spirit un-extended, yet Weiyuan is unwilling to extend it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty extends every upright spirit, yet Weiyuan refuses to extend his own.

sentences.zh: 維垣怪臣盛稱東林，以東林嘗推李三才而護熊廷弼也。

translations.literal: Weiyuan faults your subject for greatly praising the Donglin faction, on the ground that Donglin once promoted Li Sancai and shielded Xiong Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weiyuan objects that I lavish praise on the Donglin faction because it once backed Li Sancai and protected Xiong Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 抑知東林有力擊魏忠賢之楊漣，首劾崔呈秀之高攀龍乎！

translations.literal: Yet does he know that within Donglin were Yang Lian, who forcefully struck Wei Zhongxian, and Gao Panlong, who first impeached Cui Chengxiu?
translations.idiomatic: Does he not know that Donglin produced Yang Lian, who hammered Wei Zhongxian, and Gao Panlong, who led the charge against Cui Chengxiu?

sentences.zh: 忠賢窮兇極惡，維垣猶尊稱之曰「廠臣公」、「廠臣不愛錢」、「廠臣知為國為民」，而何責乎三才？

translations.literal: Zhongxian was utterly vicious in the extreme, yet Weiyuan still honored him as "Lord Factory Minister," "the Factory Minister does not love money," and "the Factory Minister knows how to serve state and people"—how then can he blame Sancai?
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was monstrous beyond measure, yet Weiyuan still hailed him as Lord Factory Minister, praised his supposed incorruptibility, and credited him with serving the realm—so how can he turn and blame Li Sancai?

sentences.zh: 五彪五虎之罪，刑官僅擬削奪，維垣不駁正，又何誅乎廷弼？

translations.literal: For the crimes of the Five Leopards and Five Tigers, the judicial officials proposed only demotion and stripping of rank, and Weiyuan did not correct them—how then can he condemn Tingbi?
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Leopards and Five Tigers were judged, the law officers proposed nothing harsher than demotion, and Weiyuan did not protest—so why demand Xiong Tingbi's head?

sentences.zh: 維垣又怪臣盛稱韓爌。

translations.literal: Weiyuan again faults your subject for greatly praising Han Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan likewise faults me for praising Han Kuang so highly.

sentences.zh: 夫舍爌昭然忤珰之大節，而加以罔利莫須有之事，已為失平。

translations.literal: To set aside Kuang's manifest great integrity in defying the eunuchs and instead attach to him the groundless charge of illicit profit is already unjust.
translations.idiomatic: To ignore Han Kuang's plain record of defying the eunuchs and smear him with a fabricated charge of greed is injustice plain and simple.

sentences.zh: 至廷弼行賄之說，乃忠賢借以誣陷清流，為楊、左諸人追贓地耳，天下誰不知，維垣猶守是說乎？

translations.literal: As for the story of Tingbi's bribery, it was merely a pretext by Zhongxian to frame the Clear Stream faction and create grounds to recover embezzled funds from Yang, Zuo, and others—who in the realm does not know this? Yet Weiyuan still clings to that story?
translations.idiomatic: The tale of Xiong Tingbi's bribes was Wei Zhongxian's tool to frame the upright and claw back "stolen" goods from Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, and their fellows—the whole world knew it—yet Weiyuan still repeats it?

sentences.zh: 維垣又怪臣盛稱文震孟。

translations.literal: Weiyuan again faults your subject for greatly praising Wen Zhenmeng.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan again faults me for praising Wen Zhenmeng so highly.

sentences.zh: 夫震孟忤珰削奪，其破帽策蹇傲蟒玉馳驛語，何可非？

translations.literal: Zhenmeng defied the eunuchs and suffered demotion and stripping of rank; his words of pride in a worn hat and lame donkey against python robes and imperial post-station rides—how can these be faulted?
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhenmeng defied the eunuchs and was stripped of office; when he boasted of his worn hat and lame donkey against courtiers in python robes racing the post roads—what fault is there in that?

sentences.zh: 維垣試觀數年來破帽策蹇之輩，較超階躐級之儔，孰為榮辱。

translations.literal: Let Weiyuan compare, over these several years, those in worn hats on lame donkeys with those who leap ranks and grades—who has honor and who shame?
translations.idiomatic: Let Weiyuan look at the men in worn hats on lame donkeys these past years beside those who vaulted over their superiors—which group bears honor, and which shame?

sentences.zh: 自此義不明，畏破帽策蹇者，相率而頌德建祠，希蟒玉馳驛者呼父、呼九千歲而不怍，可勝嘆哉！

translations.literal: Since this principle has been unclear, those who fear worn hats and lame donkeys flock to eulogize virtue and build shrines, while those who covet python robes and post-station rides call Father and Nine Thousand Years without shame—a lament beyond measure!
translations.idiomatic: Once that distinction blurred, men who feared the poverty of worn hat and lame donkey flocked to praise the powerful and build shrines to them, while men who craved python robes and post-horses cried "Father!" and "Nine thousand years!" without a blush—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 維垣又怪臣盛稱鄒元標。

translations.literal: Weiyuan again faults your subject for greatly praising Zou Yuanbiao.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan again faults me for praising Zou Yuanbiao so highly.

sentences.zh: 夫謂都門聚講為非則可，謂元標講學有他腸則不可。

translations.literal: To say that lecturing at the capital gates was wrong is arguable; to say Yuanbiao's lecturing had ulterior motives is not.
translations.idiomatic: One may argue that public lecturing at the capital was unwise; one may not claim that Zou Yuanbiao's teaching concealed some hidden agenda.

sentences.zh: 當日忠賢驅逐諸人，毀廢書院者，正欲箝學士大夫之口，恣行不義耳。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian drove out the scholars and destroyed academies, it was precisely to clamp shut the mouths of literati and officials and indulge iniquity at will.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian expelled scholars and tore down academies, his aim was to silence the educated elite and do as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 自元標以偽學見驅，而逆珰遂以真儒自命，學宮之內，儼然揖先聖為平交。

translations.literal: Since Yuanbiao was driven out on the charge of heterodox learning, the treacherous eunuchs took to calling themselves true Confucians; within the academies they bowed to the Sage as equals.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zou Yuanbiao was banished for "heterodox learning," the treacherous eunuchs styled themselves true Confucians and in the academies bowed to the Sage as though he were their peer.

sentences.zh: 使元標諸人在，豈遂至此！

translations.literal: Had Yuanbiao and his fellows still been present, would it have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Had Zou Yuanbiao and his like still been among us, would matters have sunk so low!

sentences.zh: 維垣又駁臣假借矯激。

translations.literal: Weiyuan also refutes your subject's pretended and affected vehemence.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan also attacks me for feigned and theatrical outrage.

sentences.zh: 夫當崔、魏之世，人皆任真率性，頌德建祠。

translations.literal: In the age of Cui and Wei, all were frank and unbridled in eulogizing virtue and building shrines.
translations.idiomatic: In the days of Cui Yuanbiao and Wei Zhongxian, everyone was candid and unrestrained in praising the powerful and building shrines to them.

sentences.zh: 使有一人假借矯激，而不頌不建，豈不猶賴是人哉！

translations.literal: If there were but one person who feigned vehemence and neither eulogized nor built shrines, would we not still have relied on such a person!
translations.idiomatic: If even one man only pretended outrage and refused to praise or build shrines, would we not still have owed him something!

sentences.zh: 維垣以為真小人，待其貫滿可攻去之，臣以為非計也。

translations.literal: Weiyuan holds that when a true petty man is sated, he may then be attacked and removed; your subject holds this no strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan thinks a true villain should be left until he is glutted, then driven out; I say that is no strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 必待其貫滿，其敗壞天下事已不可勝言，雖攻去之，不已晚乎！

translations.literal: Must we wait until he is sated? By then the ruin wrought upon the realm will be beyond telling; though you remove him, is it not already too late!
translations.idiomatic: Wait until he is glutted, and the harm done to the empire will be beyond reckoning—even if you remove him then, will it not be far too late?

sentences.zh: 即如崔、魏，貫滿久矣，不遇聖明，誰攻去之？

translations.literal: Take Cui and Wei: long sated they were; without encountering a sage ruler, who would have removed them?
translations.idiomatic: Look at Cui and Wei: they had been glutted for years; without a sage ruler, who could have driven them out?

sentences.zh: 維垣終以無可奈何為頌德建祠者解，臣以為非訓也。

translations.literal: Weiyuan ultimately excuses those who eulogized and built shrines as having had no choice; your subject holds this no teaching for others.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan ultimately excuses those who praised the powerful and built shrines as having had no choice; I say that is no lesson for posterity.

sentences.zh: 假令呈秀一人舞蹈稱臣於逆珰，諸臣亦以為無可奈何而從之乎？

translations.literal: Suppose Chengxiu alone performed obeisance and called himself subject to the treacherous eunuch—would the other officials also have followed, thinking they had no choice?
translations.idiomatic: If Cui Chengxiu alone had danced and called himself the treacherous eunuch's subject, would the rest of the officials also have followed, pleading they had no choice?

sentences.zh: 又令逆珰以兵劫諸臣使從叛逆，諸臣亦靡然從之，以為無可奈何而然乎？

translations.literal: Or if the treacherous eunuch had used troops to coerce the officials into rebellion—would they also have followed wholesale, thinking they had no choice?
translations.idiomatic: Or if the treacherous eunuch had used troops to force the officials into rebellion, would they likewise have gone along in droves, claiming they could do nothing else?

sentences.zh: 維垣又言「今日之忠直，不當以崔、魏為對案」，臣謂正當以崔、魏為對案也。

translations.literal: Weiyuan also says, "Today's loyalty and uprightness should not be measured against the Cui–Wei case"; your subject says they precisely should be measured against it.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan also says that today's loyal and upright men should not be judged by the Cui–Wei standard; I say they should be judged by exactly that standard.

sentences.zh: 夫人品試之崔、魏而定矣，故有東林之人，為崔、魏所恨其牴觸、畏其才望而必欲殺之逐之者，此正人也。

translations.literal: Character is tested and fixed by Cui and Wei: hence Donglin men whom Cui and Wei hated for resisting, feared for talent and reputation, and were bent on killing or driving out—these are upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Men's character is proven by how Cui and Wei treated them: Donglin men whom Cui and Wei hated for defying them, feared for their talent, and were determined to kill or exile—these are upright men.

sentences.zh: 有攻東林之人，雖為崔、魏所借，而勁節不阿，或遠或逐者，亦正人也。

translations.literal: There are men who attacked Donglin; though borrowed by Cui and Wei, yet with stiff integrity and no bending, whether exiled or driven out—these too are upright men.
translations.idiomatic: There are men who attacked Donglin; though Cui and Wei used them, if they held firm and would not bend, whether exiled or driven out, they too are upright men.

sentences.zh: 以崔、魏定邪正，猶以明鏡別妍媸。

translations.literal: To fix right and wrong by Cui and Wei is like distinguishing beauty from ugliness with a bright mirror.
translations.idiomatic: To judge right and wrong by Cui and Wei is like telling beauty from ugliness with a bright mirror.

sentences.zh: 維垣不取證於此，而安取證哉！

translations.literal: If Weiyuan does not take his proof here, from where else will he take it!
translations.idiomatic: If Weiyuan will not take his proof from this, where else will he find it!

sentences.zh: 總之東林之取憎於逆珰獨深，其得禍獨酷。

translations.literal: In sum, the Donglin faction alone incurred the treacherous eunuchs' deepest hatred and alone suffered the cruelest calamities.
translations.idiomatic: In short, the Donglin faction alone earned the treacherous eunuchs' deepest hatred and alone suffered their cruelest punishments.

sentences.zh: 在今日當曲原其被抑之苦，不當毛舉其尺寸之瑕。

translations.literal: Today we ought to make allowance for the bitterness of their suppression and not pick at every minute flaw.
translations.idiomatic: Today we should make allowance for how they were crushed, not nitpick every small fault.

sentences.zh: 乃歸逆珰以首功，代逆珰而分謗，斯亦不善立論者矣。

translations.literal: Yet to ascribe the chief merit to the treacherous eunuchs and share out their censure in their stead—this too is poor argument.
translations.idiomatic: To give the treacherous eunuchs the chief credit and share their blame in their place—that too is poor argument.

sentences.zh: 疏入，柄國者以互相詆訾兩解之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, those holding power dismissed both sides as mutual slander and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, those in power treated it as mutual slander from both sides and let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 當是時，元兇雖殛，其徒黨猶盛，無敢頌言東林者。

translations.literal: At that time, though the chief culprit had been executed, his faction remained strong, and none dared speak in praise of Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, though the chief villain had been put to death, his party remained strong, and no one dared speak well of Donglin.

sentences.zh: 自元璐疏出，清議漸明，而善類亦稍登進矣。

translations.literal: After Yuanlu's memorial appeared, clear opinion gradually prevailed, and worthy men also began to advance somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: After Ni Yuanlu's memorial appeared, honest opinion gradually clarified, and good men began to win promotion again.

sentences.zh: 元璐尋進侍講。

translations.literal: Yuanlu was soon promoted to Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Yuanlu was soon promoted to Lecturer-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，請毀《三朝要典》，言：「梃擊、紅丸、移宮三議，哄於清流，而《三朝要典》一書，成於逆豎。

translations.literal: That year in the fourth month he requested the destruction of Three Dynasties Essentials, saying: "The three controversies—the Stick Case, the Red Pill, and the Palace Shift—were argued among the Clear Stream faction, but the book Three Dynasties Essentials was compiled by treacherous minions.
translations.idiomatic: That April he asked that Three Dynasties Essentials be destroyed, writing: "The Stick Case, the Red Pill, and the Palace Shift were debated among the upright faction, but Three Dynasties Essentials was compiled by treacherous minions.

sentences.zh: 其議可兼行，其書必當速毀。

translations.literal: The debates may all be honored in turn; the book must be destroyed at once.
translations.idiomatic: The debates may all stand; the book must be destroyed without delay.

sentences.zh: 蓋當事起議興，盈廷互訟。

translations.literal: For when events arose, debates flared, and the full court wrangled.
translations.idiomatic: When each affair arose, debate flared and the whole court argued back and forth.

sentences.zh: 主梃擊者力護東宮，爭梃擊者計安神祖。

translations.literal: Advocates of the Stick Case strove to protect the Heir Apparent; opponents calculated to reassure Emperor Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: Those who upheld the Stick Case fought to protect the heir apparent; those who contested it sought to reassure Emperor Shenzong.

sentences.zh: 主紅丸者仗義之言，爭紅丸者原情之論。

translations.literal: Advocates of the Red Pill spoke in righteousness; opponents argued from human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Those who upheld the Red Pill spoke in the name of justice; those who contested it appealed to human feeling.

sentences.zh: 主移宮者弭變於幾先，爭移宮者持平於事後。

translations.literal: Advocates of the Palace Shift quelled trouble at the first sign; opponents held the balance after the fact.
translations.idiomatic: Those who upheld the Palace Shift sought to quell trouble before it spread; those who contested it held the balance once events had passed.

sentences.zh: 數者各有其是，不可偏非。

translations.literal: Each side had its point; none should be wholly condemned.
translations.idiomatic: Each side had its truth; none should be condemned outright.

sentences.zh: 總在逆珰未用之先，雖甚水火，不害塤篪，此一局也。

translations.literal: All this was before the treacherous eunuchs put the cases to use; however sharp the conflict, it did not harm harmony like pipes and flutes—this was one phase.
translations.idiomatic: All this was before the treacherous eunuchs weaponized the cases; however fierce the quarrel, it did not destroy harmony like clashing pipes—this was one phase.

sentences.zh: 既而楊漣二十四罪之疏發，魏廣微此輩門戶之說興，於是逆珰殺人則借三案，群小求富貴則借三案。

translations.literal: Then came Yang Lian's memorial listing twenty-four crimes, and the factional talk of Wei Guangwei and his ilk arose; thereafter the treacherous eunuchs killed by borrowing the Three Cases, and petty men sought wealth and rank by borrowing the Three Cases.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Yang Lian's memorial of twenty-four crimes and the factional rhetoric of Wei Guangwei and his like; from then on the treacherous eunuchs killed by wielding the Three Cases, and petty men sought wealth and rank by wielding them too.

sentences.zh: 經此二借，而三案全非矣。

translations.literal: After these two borrowings, the Three Cases were wholly corrupted.
translations.idiomatic: After these two abuses, the Three Cases were utterly perverted.

sentences.zh: 故凡推慈歸孝於先皇，正其頌德稱功於義父，又一局也。

translations.literal: Thus all who pressed filial kindness on the late emperor and who eulogized and praised their godfather—that was another phase.
translations.idiomatic: Then came those who pressed filial piety on the late emperor and praised their "godfather"—that was another phase.

sentences.zh: 網已密而猶疑有遺鱗，勢已重而或憂其翻局。

translations.literal: The net was already tight yet they still feared a fish escaping; their power was already heavy yet they sometimes worried the game would turn.
translations.idiomatic: Their net was already tight, yet they still feared a fish had slipped through; their power was already great, yet they still worried the game might turn.

sentences.zh: 崔、魏諸奸始創立私編，標題《要典》，以之批根今日，則眾正之黨碑；

translations.literal: The villains Cui and Wei first compiled a private work titled Essentials to root out opponents today—making it a stele listing the righteous.
translations.idiomatic: The villains Cui and Wei first compiled a private work called Essentials; used to attack opponents today, it became a stele of the righteous.

sentences.zh: 以之免死他年，即上公之鐵券。

translations.literal: Used to secure immunity from death in years to come, it was their iron certificate of grace.
translations.idiomatic: Used to secure immunity in years to come, it was their iron certificate of grace.

sentences.zh: 又一局也。

translations.literal: Yet another phase.
translations.idiomatic: That was yet another phase.

sentences.zh: 由此而觀，三案者，天下之公議；

translations.literal: Viewed thus, the Three Cases are the public judgment of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, the Three Cases are the public judgment of the realm.

sentences.zh: 《要典》者，魏氏之私書。

translations.literal: Essentials is the Wei clan's private book.
translations.idiomatic: Essentials is the Wei faction's private book.

sentences.zh: 三案自三案，《要典》自《要典》也。

translations.literal: The Three Cases are the Three Cases; Essentials is Essentials.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Cases are one thing; Essentials is another.

sentences.zh: 今為金石不刊之論者，誠未深思。

translations.literal: Those who now treat it as an immutable verdict have truly not thought deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Those who now treat it as an unalterable verdict have not thought the matter through.

sentences.zh: 臣謂翻即紛囂，改亦多事，惟有毀之而已。」

translations.literal: Your subject holds that to overturn it would stir uproar, to revise it would be troublesome—there is only to destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that to overturn it would stir uproar and to revise it would be burdensome; there is only to destroy it.

sentences.zh: 帝命禮部會詞臣詳議。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of the memorial; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to convene the academicians for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: End of quoted memorial; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to convene the academicians for full deliberation.

sentences.zh: 議上，遂焚其板。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, they burned the printing blocks.
translations.idiomatic: When their report was submitted, the printing blocks were burned.

sentences.zh: 侍講孫之獬，忠賢黨也，聞之，詣閣大哭，天下笑之。

translations.literal: Lecturer Sun Zhixi, a partisan of Zhongxian, hearing of it, went to the Grand Secretariat and wept aloud; the realm laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturer Sun Zhixi, a partisan of Wei Zhongxian, heard the news, went to the Grand Secretariat, and wept aloud; the whole world laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 元璐歷遷南京司業、右中允。

translations.literal: Yuanlu was successively promoted to Vice Director of Studies at Nanjing and Right Assistant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Yuanlu rose in turn to Vice Director of Studies at Nanjing and Right Assistant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 四年，進右諭德，充日講官，進右庶子。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced to Right Tutor, appointed Daily Lecturer, and advanced to Right Supervisor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Right Tutor, appointed Daily Lecturer, and then to Right Supervisor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 上制實八策：曰間插部，曰繕京邑，曰優守兵，曰靖降人，曰益寇餉，曰儲邊才，曰奠輦轂，曰嚴教育。

translations.literal: He presented eight substantive policies: interspersing ministries, repairing the capital, favoring garrison troops, pacifying surrendered peoples, increasing bandit-suppression funds, storing border talent, securing the imperial carriage, and tightening education.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted eight substantive policies: reorganizing ministries, repairing the capital, strengthening garrison troops, pacifying surrendered peoples, increasing bandit-suppression funds, cultivating border talent, securing the capital region, and tightening education.

sentences.zh: 又上制虛八策：曰端政本，曰伸公議，曰宣義問，曰一條教，曰慮久遠，曰昭激勸，曰勵名節，曰假體貌。

translations.literal: He also presented eight formal policies: rectifying the political foundation, extending public opinion, spreading righteous inquiry, unifying instruction, planning for the long term, clarifying incentives, encouraging integrity of name, and lending proper dignity.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted eight formal policies: rectifying the political foundation, extending public debate, spreading moral inquiry, unifying instruction, planning for the long term, clarifying rewards and punishments, encouraging integrity, and restoring proper dignity to office.

sentences.zh: 其端政本，悉規切溫體仁；

translations.literal: In rectifying the foundation, he entirely admonished Wen Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: In rectifying the foundation, he admonished Wen Tiren throughout.

sentences.zh: 其伸公議，則詆張捷薦呂純如謀翻逆案事。

translations.literal: In extending public opinion, he denounced Zhang Jie's recommending Lü Chunru to overturn the treason cases.
translations.idiomatic: In extending public debate, he denounced Zhang Jie for recommending Lü Chunru to overturn the treason cases.

sentences.zh: 捷大怒，上疏力攻，元璐疏辨，帝俱不問。

translations.literal: Jie was furious and memorialized in force; Yuanlu memorialized in defense; the emperor took no notice of either.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie was furious and memorialized in attack; Ni Yuanlu memorialized in reply; the emperor ignored both.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Chancellor of the National Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Chancellor of the National Academy.

sentences.zh: 元璐雅負時望，位漸通顯。

translations.literal: Yuanlu had long borne the hopes of his age, and his rank gradually rose to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Yuanlu had long enjoyed public esteem, and his rank gradually rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 帝意向之，深為體仁所忌。

translations.literal: The emperor inclined toward him, and Tiren deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored him, and Wen Tiren deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝手書其名下閣，令以履歷進，體仁益恐。

translations.literal: One day the emperor wrote his name by hand and sent it to the Grand Secretariat, ordering his résumé forwarded; Tiren grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor wrote his name by hand and sent it to the Grand Secretariat, ordering his record forwarded; Wen Tiren grew still more afraid.

sentences.zh: 會誠意伯劉孔昭謀掌戎政，體仁餌孔昭使攻元璐，言其妻陳尚存，而妾王冒繼配復封，敗禮亂法。

translations.literal: As Honorary Marquis Liu Kongzhao sought military command, Tiren baited Kongzhao to attack Yuanlu, saying his wife Chen still lived while concubine Wang falsely claimed succession and reinstatement, violating ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: When Honorary Marquis Liu Kongzhao sought military command, Wen Tiren baited him to attack Ni Yuanlu, alleging that his wife Chen still lived while concubine Wang had falsely claimed succession and reinstatement, violating ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 詔下吏部核奏，其同里尚書姜逢元，侍郎王業浩、劉宗周及其從兄御史元珙，鹹言陳氏以過被出，繼娶王非妾，體仁意沮。

translations.literal: An edict went to the Ministry of Personnel for verification; fellow-townsmen Minister Jiang Fengyuan, Vice Ministers Wang Yehao and Liu Zongzhou, and his cousin Censor Yuan Gong all said Chen had been expelled for faults and Wang was a lawful remarriage, not a concubine; Tiren's intent was thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went to the Ministry of Personnel for investigation; his fellow-townsmen Minister Jiang Fengyuan, Vice Ministers Wang Yehao and Liu Zongzhou, and his cousin Censor Yuan Gong all testified that Chen had been divorced for misconduct and that Wang was a lawful second wife, not a concubine; Wen Tiren's scheme faltered.

sentences.zh: 會部議行撫按勘奏，即擬旨云：「登科錄二氏並列，罪跡顯然，何待行勘。」

translations.literal: When the ministry proposed investigation by provincial officials, he immediately drafted the rescript: "The examination register lists both families; the offense is plain—why wait for investigation?
translations.idiomatic: When the ministry proposed an investigation by provincial officials, he immediately drafted the rescript: "The examination register lists both families side by side; the offense is plain—why wait for an inquiry?

sentences.zh: 遂落職閑住。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of the rescript; Yuanlu was thus dismissed to idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: End of quoted rescript; Ni Yuanlu was dismissed from office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 孔昭京營不可得，遂以南京操江償之。

translations.literal: Kongzhao could not obtain the capital army command and was compensated with the Nanjing river patrol post instead.
translations.idiomatic: Kongzhao could not obtain command of the capital army and was given the Nanjing river patrol post instead.

sentences.zh: 十五年九月，詔起兵部右侍郎兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year he was ordered raised to Vice Minister of War with concurrent Reader-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year he was ordered appointed Vice Minister of War with concurrent Reader-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 明年春抵都，陳制敵機宜，帝喜。

translations.literal: The next spring he reached the capital, set forth expedients against the enemy, and the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he reached the capital, laid out plans against the enemy, and the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 五月，超拜戶部尚書兼翰林院學士，仍充日講官。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was exceptionally promoted to Minister of Revenue with concurrent Academician of the Hanlin Academy, still serving as Daily Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was exceptionally promoted to Minister of Revenue with concurrent Hanlin Academician, while continuing as Daily Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 祖制，浙人不得官戶部。

translations.literal: By ancestral regulation, men from Zhejiang might not hold the Revenue post.
translations.idiomatic: By ancestral regulation, men from Zhejiang were barred from the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 元璐辭，不許。

translations.literal: Yuanlu declined; he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Yuanlu declined; the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 帝眷元璐甚，五日三賜對。

translations.literal: The emperor favored Yuanlu greatly, granting him audience three times in five days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Ni Yuanlu greatly, granting him audience three times in five days.

sentences.zh: 因奏：「陛下誠用臣，臣請得參兵部謀。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "If Your Majesty truly employs your subject, your subject asks leave to join the Ministry of War in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "If Your Majesty truly means to use me, I ask leave to join the Ministry of War in planning.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「已諭樞臣，令與卿協計。」

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of the memorial; the emperor said: "I have already instructed the military chiefs to cooperate with you in planning."
translations.idiomatic: End of quoted memorial; the emperor said: "I have already told the military chiefs to work with you in planning."

sentences.zh: 當是時，馮元飆為兵部，與元璐同誌，鉤考兵食，中外想望治平。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of the imperial reply; at that time Feng Yuanying headed the Ministry of War; sharing Yuanlu's aims, they audited troops and grain, and within and without the court hope looked toward good governance.
translations.idiomatic: End of quoted reply; at that time Feng Yuanying headed the Ministry of War; sharing Ni Yuanlu's aims, they audited troops and supplies, and court and country looked toward better times.

sentences.zh: 惟帝亦以用兩人晚，而時事益不可為，左支右詘，既已無可奈何。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor too knew he had employed the two men late; affairs grew harder to manage, and he braced himself on either side already helpless.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor too knew he had employed the two men too late; affairs grew ever harder to manage, and he was already stretched beyond remedy.

sentences.zh: 故事，諸邊餉司悉中差，元璐請改為大差，兼兵部銜，令清核軍伍，不稱職者即遣人代之。

translations.literal: By precedent all border pay offices were filled by mid-ranking dispatch; Yuanlu asked to change them to senior dispatch with concurrent War Ministry title, to audit armies clearly, and replace incompetents at once.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent all border pay offices were filled by mid-ranking envoys; Ni Yuanlu asked that they be changed to senior envoys with concurrent War Ministry rank, to audit armies clearly and replace incompetents immediately.

sentences.zh: 先是，屢遣科臣出督四方租賦，元璐以為擾民無益，罷之，而專責撫按。

translations.literal: Previously censors had repeatedly been sent to supervise rents and levies in all quarters; Yuanlu held this harassed the people without benefit, abolished it, and charged governors alone.
translations.idiomatic: Previously censors had repeatedly been sent to supervise rents and levies throughout the realm; Ni Yuanlu held this harassed the people without benefit, abolished the practice, and charged provincial governors alone.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎莊祖誨督剿寇餉，憂為盜劫，遠避之長沙、衡州。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zhuang Zuhui supervised bandit-suppression funds, fearing robbery by bandits, and fled far to Changsha and Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zhuang Zuhui, charged with supervising bandit-suppression funds, feared robbery by bandits and fled as far as Changsha and Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 元璐請令督撫自催，毋煩朝使。

translations.literal: Yuanlu asked that governors and commanders collect funds themselves without troubling court emissaries.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Yuanlu asked that governors and commanders collect funds themselves without troubling court emissaries.

sentences.zh: 自軍興以來，正供之外，有邊餉，有新餉，有練餉，款目多，黠吏易為奸，元璐請合為一。

translations.literal: Since the armies mobilized, beyond regular delivery there were border pay, new pay, and drill pay—many categories in which crafty clerks easily committed fraud; Yuanlu asked they be merged into one.
translations.idiomatic: Since the armies mobilized, beyond regular taxes there were border pay, new pay, and drill pay—so many categories that crafty clerks easily cheated the state; Ni Yuanlu asked that they be merged into one.

sentences.zh: 帝皆報可。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 時國用益詘，而災傷蠲免又多。

translations.literal: At that time state revenue grew ever more strained, while disaster relief and tax remissions also increased.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury was shrinking, yet tax forgiveness for flood and famine only grew.

sentences.zh: 元璐計無所出，請開贖罪例，且令到官滿歲者，得輸貲給封誥。

translations.literal: Yuanlu could find no solution and asked to open the commutation-of-punishment statute, and to allow officials who had served a full year in post to pay for patents of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Yuanlu could find no other way and asked to open the commutation-of-punishment statute, and to let officials who had served a full year in post pay for patents of honor.

sentences.zh: 帝亦從之。

translations.literal: The emperor also assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented to these as well.

sentences.zh: 先是，有崇明人沈廷揚者，獻海運策，元璐奏聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shen Tingyang of Chongming had presented a sea-transport plan; Yuanlu memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shen Tingyang of Chongming had presented a plan for transport by sea; Ni Yuanlu reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 命試行，乃以廟灣船六艘聽運進。

translations.literal: Ordered to trial, six Miao Bay vessels were placed at his disposal for transport to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a trial run, and six Miao Bay vessels were placed at his disposal to carry grain to the capital.

sentences.zh: 月余，廷揚見元璐，元璐驚曰：「我已奏聞上，謂公去矣，何在此？」

translations.literal: After more than a month Tingyang called on Yuanlu; Yuanlu exclaimed: "I have already reported to His Majesty that you had gone—why are you here?
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month Shen Tingyang called on Ni Yuanlu; Yuanlu exclaimed: "I have already told His Majesty you had gone—why are you still here?

sentences.zh: 廷揚曰：「已去復來矣，運已至。」

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of Yuanlu's speech; Tingyang said: "I went and have returned; the cargo has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: End of Yuanlu's quoted speech; Tingyang said: "I went and have returned; the grain has arrived."

sentences.zh: 元璐又驚喜聞上。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of Tingyang's speech; Yuanlu again, astonished and delighted, reported to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: End of Tingyang's quoted speech; Ni Yuanlu, astonished and delighted, reported the news to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上亦喜，命酌議。

translations.literal: The emperor too was pleased and ordered deliberation over wine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was likewise delighted and ordered the matter discussed at leisure.

sentences.zh: 乃議歲糧艘，漕與海各相半行焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon they deliberated the year's grain vessels: canal transport and sea transport each to proceed half and half.
translations.idiomatic: They then settled on sending that year's grain fleet half by the Grand Canal and half by sea.

sentences.zh: 十月，命兼攝吏部事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he was ordered to take on concurrently the affairs of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was ordered to serve concurrently as acting head of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 陳演忌元璐，風魏藻德言於帝曰：「元璐書生，不習錢谷。」

translations.literal: Chen Yan resented Yuanlu and prompted Wei Zaode to tell the emperor: "Yuanlu is a bookish man and unpracticed in revenue and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan, who bore a grudge against Ni Yuanlu, incited Wei Zaode to tell the emperor: "Yuanlu is merely a scholar and knows nothing of fiscal administration.

sentences.zh: 元璐亦數請解職。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of Chen Yan's speech; Yuanlu also repeatedly requested to be relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: End of the quoted accusation relayed through Wei Zaode; Ni Yuanlu likewise petitioned several times to resign his post.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月，命以原官專直日講。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year, he was ordered to keep his original office and attend solely to daily lectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year of Chongzhen he was ordered to retain his existing rank and devote himself exclusively to the daily lecture duty before the throne.

sentences.zh: 逾月，李自成陷京師，元璐整衣冠拜闕，大書幾上曰：「南都尚可為。

translations.literal: After a month, Li Zicheng captured the capital; Yuanlu straightened cap and gown, bowed toward the palace, and wrote large on the table: "The Southern Capital can still be made to serve.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Li Zicheng took Beijing; Ni Yuanlu arrayed his hat and robes, bowed toward the palace, and wrote in large characters on his desk: "Nanjing can still be saved.

sentences.zh: 死，吾分也，勿以衣衾斂。

translations.literal: Death is my allotted portion; do not wrap me in garments and bedding.
translations.idiomatic: To die is my duty; do not shroud me in robes and covers.

sentences.zh: 暴我屍，聊誌吾痛。」

translations.literal: Expose my corpse, merely to record my grief.
translations.idiomatic: Leave my body exposed, that my anguish may somehow be witnessed.

sentences.zh: 遂南向坐，取帛自縊而死。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of his testament; thereupon he sat facing south, took silk, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: End of his written testament; he then sat facing south, took a length of silk, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，吏部尚書，謚文正。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted Junior Tutor and Minister of Personnel; posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the ranks of Junior Tutor and Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Wenzheng, "Upright in Culture."

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚文正。

translations.literal: This dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty likewise conferred upon him the posthumous title Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 李邦華，字孟暗，吉水人。

translations.literal: Li Banghua, style Meng'an, a man of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua, whose style was Meng'an, came from Jishui in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 受業同里鄒元標，與父廷諫同舉萬歷三十一年鄉試。

translations.literal: He received instruction from his townsman Zou Yuanbiao and, together with his father Tingjian, passed the provincial examination in the thirty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under his fellow townsman Zou Yuanbiao and, together with his father Li Tingjian, passed the provincial examination in the thirty-first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 父子自相鏃礪，布衣徒步赴公車。

translations.literal: Father and son whetted one another like grindstone and blade, went in plain cloth and on foot to the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son sharpened each other like blade on stone and set out for the capital examinations in plain dress and on foot.

sentences.zh: 明年，邦華成進士，授涇縣知縣，有異政。

translations.literal: The next year Banghua became a jinshi, was appointed magistrate of Jing County, and had exceptional administration.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Li Banghua passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed magistrate of Jing County, where his governance won unusual praise.

sentences.zh: 行取，擬授御史。

translations.literal: Selected for promotion from local service; it was proposed to appoint him investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected for central appointment from local service and was slated to receive a post as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 值黨論初起，朝士多詆顧憲成，邦華與相拄，遂指目邦華東林。

translations.literal: It happened that factional debate was just rising; court officials mostly denounced Gu Xiancheng, and Banghua opposed them, so eyes were fixed on Banghua as Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: Factional strife was then just beginning; most court officials were attacking Gu Xiancheng, and Li Banghua stood against them, whereupon he was marked out as a man of the Donglin faction.

sentences.zh: 以是，越二年而後拜命，陳法祖用人十事：曰內閣不當專用詞臣，曰詞臣不當專守館局，曰詞臣不當教習內書堂，曰六科都給事中不當內外間阻，曰御史升遷不當概論考滿，曰吏部乞假不當積至正郎，曰關倉諸差不當專用舉貢任子，曰調簡推知不當驟遷京秩，曰進士改教不當概從內轉，曰邊方州縣不當盡用鄉貢。

translations.literal: Because of this, only after two more years did he receive appointment; he set forth ten matters on appointing men: that the Grand Secretariat should not employ Hanlin scholars exclusively; that Hanlin scholars should not remain solely in the Academy bureau; that Hanlin scholars should not instruct in the Inner Writing Hall; that the six chiefs of the investigating censors should not be obstructed between inner and outer court; that censors' promotions should not be judged solely by completion of term; that the Ministry of Personnel's leave petitions should not pile up until one reached director rank; that customs-house and related posts should not employ solely tribute students through hereditary appointment; that transferred and recommended prefectural magistrates should not abruptly rise to capital ranks; that jinshi who became instructors should not invariably be transferred inward; that frontier prefectures and counties should not all employ provincial graduates.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason his formal appointment came only two years later. In his memorial he set forth ten reforms for official selection: the Grand Secretariat ought not to rely exclusively on Hanlin academicians; Hanlin academicians ought not to remain permanently in the Hanlin Academy; Hanlin academicians ought not to teach in the Inner Writing Hall; the six supervising secretaries-in-chief should not be blocked between palace and bureaucracy; promotions of censors should not be decided merely by completion of a tour of duty; leave applications at the Ministry of Personnel should not be allowed to accumulate until an official reached full directorship; customs and warehouse posts should not be filled only by tribute-student hereditary appointments; magistrates transferred in from other circuits should not be rushed into capital posts; jinshi assigned as instructors should not invariably be brought inside the capital; and frontier prefectures and counties should not be staffed entirely with provincial graduates.

sentences.zh: 疏上，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial went up; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was submitted, but the throne gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，福王之藩已有期，忽傳旨莊田務足四萬頃。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, the Prince of Fu's departure to his fief already had a fixed date, when suddenly an edict was transmitted that manor lands must reach forty thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Wanli, the date for the Prince of Fu to take up his fief had already been set, when suddenly an edict demanded that his estate lands must amount to forty thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 廷臣相顧愕眙，計田數必不足，則期將復更，然無敢抗言爭之者。

translations.literal: Court ministers looked at one another in stunned silence, reckoned the acreage must fall short and the date would be changed again, yet none dared speak out in protest.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers stared at one another in dismay, calculating that the required acreage could not be met and the schedule would have to slip again, yet no one dared openly object.

sentences.zh: 邦華首疏諫，廷臣乃相繼爭，期得毋易。

translations.literal: Banghua was first to memorialize in remonstrance; court ministers then followed in contention, and the date was not altered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua led with a memorial of remonstrance, and other officials followed in protest, so the scheduled date was left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 巡視銀庫，上祛弊十事，中貴不便，格不行。

translations.literal: Inspecting the silver vaults, he submitted ten measures to remove abuses; palace eunuchs found it inconvenient, and it was blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the silver vaults he submitted ten proposals to eliminate abuses; the palace eunuchs found them inconvenient, and the measures were blocked and never implemented.

sentences.zh: 巡按浙江，織造中官劉成死，命歸其事於有司，別遣中官呂貴錄成遺貲。

translations.literal: Touring Zhejiang as investigating censor, the eunuch Liu Cheng of the weaving directorate died; the court ordered the matter returned to civil officials and separately sent the eunuch Lü Gui to inventory Cheng's hoard.
translations.idiomatic: On his tour as investigating censor in Zhejiang, the eunuch Liu Cheng, who supervised the imperial silk workshops, died; the court ordered civil officials to take over the work and separately dispatched the eunuch Lü Gui to inventory Cheng's seized assets.

sentences.zh: 貴族奸民紀光詭稱機戶，詣闕保留貴代成督造。

translations.literal: Gui instigated his clique and a wicked commoner, Ji Guang, who falsely claimed to be a loom-house master and went to the palace to petition that Gui be retained to replace Cheng in supervising manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gui incited his followers and a scheming commoner named Ji Guang, who falsely claimed to represent the loom masters and went to court to petition that Gui be kept on to replace Cheng as supervisor of the workshops.

sentences.zh: 邦華極論二人交關作奸罪。

translations.literal: Banghua vigorously argued the crime of the two men's collusion in wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua forcefully denounced the pair for conspiring in fraud.

sentences.zh: 光疏不由通政，不下內閣，以中旨行之。

translations.literal: Guang's memorial did not go through the Transmission Office, did not go down to the Grand Secretariat, and was carried out by a palace edict.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Guang's petition bypassed the Transmission Office and the Grand Secretariat alike, and the appointment was executed by a direct edict from the palace.

sentences.zh: 邦華三疏爭，皆不報。

translations.literal: Banghua contested in three memorials; all went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua submitted three further memorials of protest, and none received a reply.

sentences.zh: 是時神宗好貨，中官有所進奉，名為孝順。

translations.literal: At this time Shenzong loved wealth; eunuchs made offerings called "filial submission."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Wanli Emperor was greedy for revenue, and eunuchs would present gifts to him under the name of "filial offerings."

sentences.zh: 疏中刺及之，並劾左右大奄之黨貴者，於是期滿久不得代。

translations.literal: His memorial also stabbed at this and impeached powerful eunuchs on the ruler's flanks; thereupon when his term ended he long could not be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial also struck at this practice and impeached the powerful eunuchs surrounding the throne; as a result, when his tour of duty ended he was long denied a successor and could not leave his post.

sentences.zh: 四十四年引疾歸。
