translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 時群小力排東林，指鄒元標為黨魁。

translations.literal: At the time petty men fiercely excluded the Donglin faction and pointed to Zou Yuanbiao as faction head.
translations.idiomatic: Petty officials were then pressing hard against the Donglin faction and named Zou Yuanbiao as its ringleader.

sentences.zh: 邦華與元標同里，相師友，又性好別黑白。

translations.literal: Banghua and Yuanbiao were from the same district, teacher and friend to each other, and he by nature loved to distinguish black from white.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua was a fellow townsman of Zou Yuanbiao and his close student and friend, and by nature he insisted on drawing sharp moral lines.

sentences.zh: 或勸其委蛇，邦華曰：「寧為偏枯之學問，不作反覆之小人。」

translations.literal: Some urged him to bend and yield; Banghua said: "Better one-sided, withered learning than a back-and-forth petty man.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged him to bend with the times, Li Banghua said: "I would rather hold to a one-sided and rigid integrity than become a man who shifts with every wind.

sentences.zh: 聞者益嫉之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of Banghua's speech; those who heard hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: End of his quoted reply; those who heard him only hated him the more.

sentences.zh: 明年以年例出為山東參議。

translations.literal: The next year, by the seniority rule, he went out as Shandong Assistant Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, under the routine for officials of long service, he was posted out as Assistant Administration Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 其父廷諫時為南京刑部郎中，亦罷歸。

translations.literal: His father Tingjian was then a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and had also been dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Tingjian was then a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and had likewise been dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 邦華乃辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: Banghua thereupon pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua therefore pleaded illness and declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年起故官，飭易州兵備。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he was restored to his former office and drilled the military preparedness of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianqi reign he was restored to his former rank and put in charge of drilling the defenses of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年遷光祿少卿，即還家省父。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and immediately returned home to visit his father.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and at once went home to attend to his father.

sentences.zh: 四月，擢右僉都御史，代畢自嚴巡撫天津。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and replaced Bi Ziyan as Grand Coordinator of Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was elevated to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and succeeded Bi Ziyan as Grand Coordinator of Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 軍府新立，庶務草創，邦華至，極力振飭，津門軍遂為諸鎮冠。

translations.literal: The military headquarters was newly established and all affairs rudimentary; when Banghua arrived he vigorously restored order, and the Tianjin garrison troops thereupon became first among all commands.
translations.idiomatic: The military headquarters had only just been established and every affair was still rudimentary; when Li Banghua arrived he threw himself into reform, and the Tianjin garrison soon ranked first among all frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 進兵部右侍郎，復還家省父。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of War and again returned home to visit his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of War and once more went home to care for his father.

sentences.zh: 四年夏抵京，奄黨大嘩，謂樞輔孫承宗以萬壽節入覲，將清君側之惡，邦華實召之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year he reached the capital; the eunuch faction raised a great uproar, saying Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong was entering audience on the Longevity Festival to purge evil beside the ruler, and that Banghua had really summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year he reached the capital, and the eunuch faction raised a furious outcry, claiming that Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong was coming to court for the emperor's birthday to purge the evil at the ruler's side—and that Li Banghua had summoned him to do it.

sentences.zh: 乃立勒承宗還鎮，邦華引疾去。

translations.literal: Thereupon they immediately compelled Chengzong back to his command; Banghua pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: They at once forced Sun Chengzong back to his frontier command, and Li Banghua resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，奄黨劾削其官。

translations.literal: The next autumn the eunuch faction impeached him and stripped his office.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn the eunuch faction impeached him and stripped him of his rank.

sentences.zh: 京營故有占役、虛冒之弊。

translations.literal: The capital garrison had long had the abuses of occupied service and false rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The capital garrison had long suffered from the abuses of commandeered labor and fictitious muster rolls.

sentences.zh: 占役者，其人為諸將所役，一小營至四五百人，且有賣閑、包操諸弊。

translations.literal: As to occupied service: the men were used by various generals; a single small camp might reach four or five hundred men, and there were also abuses of selling idle time and contracting drill by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: Under occupied service, soldiers were pressed into private service by generals; a single small camp might swell to four or five hundred men, with further abuses such as selling off duty time and hiring substitutes for drill.

sentences.zh: 虛冒者，無其人，諸將及勛戚、奄寺、豪強以蒼頭冒選鋒壯丁，月支厚餉。

translations.literal: As to false rolls: there were no such men; generals, meritorious kin, eunuch temples, and powerful families used house servants to pose as selected crack troops and sturdy youths, drawing thick monthly pay.
translations.idiomatic: Under false rolls, no real soldiers existed at all: generals, noble clans, eunuch establishments, and local magnates listed household servants as elite vanguard troops and drew lavish monthly pay for them.

sentences.zh: 邦華核還占役萬，清虛冒千。

translations.literal: Banghua verified and returned ten thousand occupied-service men and cleared out one thousand false rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua audited the rolls and restored ten thousand men from illegal private service while eliminating one thousand fictitious names.

sentences.zh: 三大營軍十余萬，半老弱。

translations.literal: The three great camps had more than a hundred thousand troops, half of them old and weak.
translations.idiomatic: The three great camps mustered more than a hundred thousand men, yet half were aged or infirm.

sentences.zh: 故事，軍缺聽告補，率由賄得。

translations.literal: By precedent, vacancies in the ranks might be filled on petition, and as a rule were obtained through bribery.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, vacancies could be filled on application, and as a rule appointments were bought with bribes.

sentences.zh: 邦華必親校，非年壯力強者不錄，自是軍鮮冒濫。

translations.literal: Banghua always examined recruits in person; none but the young and strong were enrolled, and from then on the army rarely had false or excessive enrollment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua personally inspected every recruit; only the young and strong were accepted, and from then on fraudulent enlistment became rare.

sentences.zh: 三營選鋒萬，壯丁七千，餉倍他軍，而疲弱不異。

translations.literal: The three camps' selected vanguard numbered ten thousand, sturdy youths seven thousand; pay was double that of other armies, yet weakness was no different.
translations.idiomatic: The elite vanguard of the three camps numbered ten thousand men and the sturdy youths seven thousand; their pay was double that of ordinary troops, yet they were no less feeble.

sentences.zh: 邦華下令，每把總兵五百，月自簡五人，年必二十五以下，力必二百五十斤以上，技必兼弓矢火炮，月一解送，補選鋒壯丁之缺，自是人人思奮。

translations.literal: Banghua issued an order: each company commander of five hundred was monthly to select five men himself; age must be below twenty-five, strength above two hundred fifty jin, skill must combine bow, arrow, and cannon; once a month they were sent up to fill vacancies among the selected vanguard and sturdy youths—from then on every man thought to strive.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua ordered that every company commander of five hundred men should each month personally select five recruits under twenty-five years of age, able to lift at least two hundred fifty jin, and trained in both archery and artillery; each month these men were forwarded to fill vacancies in the elite ranks, and from then on every soldier strove to excel.

sentences.zh: 三大營領六副將，又分三十六營，官以三百六十七人計，所用掾史皆積猾。

translations.literal: The three great camps were led by six vice generals and further divided into thirty-six camps; officials numbered three hundred sixty-seven in all, and the clerks employed were all long-seasoned rogues.
translations.idiomatic: The three great camps were commanded by six deputy generals and subdivided into thirty-six battalions, with three hundred sixty-seven officers in all; the clerks they employed were veteran schemers.

sentences.zh: 邦華按罪十余人，又行一歲二考察之令，自是諸奸為戢。

translations.literal: Banghua prosecuted more than ten men on criminal charges and also implemented the rule of two inspections per year; from then on the various villains were restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua punished more than a dozen offenders and instituted biannual performance reviews; from then on the worst abuses were curbed.

sentences.zh: 營馬額二萬六千，至是止萬五千。

translations.literal: The camp horse quota was twenty-six thousand; by this time only fifteen thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: The authorized strength of camp horses was twenty-six thousand, but by this time only fifteen thousand remained on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 他官公事得借騎，總督、協理及巡視科道，例有坐班馬，不肖且折橐入錢，營馬大耗。

translations.literal: Other officials on public business might borrow mounts; the grand coordinator, co-administrator, and touring censors by rule had desk-duty horses, while the unworthy even broke open purses to take money—camp horses were greatly depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Other officials on public business were allowed to borrow mounts, and the grand coordinator, co-administrator, and touring censors all had horses assigned for routine duty; the unscrupulous even extorted cash for loans, and camp horses were squandered on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 邦華首減己班馬三之一，他官借馬，非公事不得騎，自是濫借為希。

translations.literal: Banghua first reduced his own desk-duty horses by one third; other officials borrowing horses might not ride them except on public business—from then on abusive borrowing became rare.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua began by cutting his own assigned horses by one third, and ruled that other officials might borrow camp horses only for genuine public business; abusive borrowing thereafter became uncommon.

sentences.zh: 京營歲領太仆銀萬六千兩，屯田籽粒銀千六十兩，犒軍制器胥徒工食取給焉。

translations.literal: The capital garrison yearly received sixteen thousand taels from the Court of the Imperial Stud and one thousand sixty taels of grain-seed silver from garrison fields; rewards to troops, manufacture of weapons, clerks, laborers, and rations were all supplied from these.
translations.idiomatic: The capital garrison received sixteen thousand taels yearly from the Court of the Imperial Stud and another one thousand sixty taels from its garrison fields; troop rewards, arms production, clerks, laborers, and rations all depended on these funds.

sentences.zh: 各官取之無度，歲用不敷。

translations.literal: Various officials took from them without measure, and yearly expenditure could not cover needs.
translations.idiomatic: Officials drew on these funds without restraint, and every year the budget fell short.

sentences.zh: 邦華建議，先協理歲取千四百，總督巡視遞節減，自是營帑遂裕。

translations.literal: Banghua proposed that the co-administrator first reduce his yearly draw by fourteen hundred, and the grand coordinator and touring inspectors reduce theirs in turn; from then on the camp treasury became ample.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua proposed that the co-administrator first cut his annual draw by fourteen hundred taels, with the grand coordinator and touring inspectors reducing theirs in turn; the garrison treasury thereafter became solvent.

sentences.zh: 營將三百六十，聽用者稱是。

translations.literal: Camp generals numbered three hundred sixty; those who heard of his measures approved.
translations.idiomatic: There were three hundred sixty camp officers in all, and those who served under him approved of his reforms.

sentences.zh: 一官缺，請托紛至。

translations.literal: When one office fell vacant, petitions and entreaties poured in.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a post fell vacant, favor-seekers swarmed in with petitions.

sentences.zh: 邦華悉杜絕，行計日省成法。

translations.literal: Banghua shut them all out and implemented the method of daily accounting by scheduled completion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua shut them all out and instituted a system of daily progress accounting for every task.

sentences.zh: 每小營各置簿，月上事狀於協理，以定殿最。

translations.literal: Each small camp kept its own register; monthly it submitted reports of affairs to the co-administrator to fix merit and demerit.
translations.idiomatic: Each small camp kept its own ledger and submitted monthly reports to the co-administrator, who used them to rank performance.

sentences.zh: 舊制，三大營外復設三備兵營，營三千人，餉視正軍，而不習技擊，益為豪家隱冒。

translations.literal: By old regulation, outside the three great camps three reserve troop camps were also established, three thousand men per camp, pay equal to regular troops, yet they did not practice fighting skills and became all the more a place for powerful families to hide false rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, three reserve battalions of three thousand men each had been set up outside the three great camps; they received regular pay but received no combat training and served chiefly as a cover for powerful families to pad the rolls.

sentences.zh: 邦華核去四千余人，又汰老弱千，疏請歸並三大營不另設，由是戎政大厘。

translations.literal: Banghua verified and removed more than four thousand men, also cut out one thousand old and weak, memorialized requesting merger back into the three great camps without separate establishment; thereby military administration was greatly set in order.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua struck more than four thousand names from the rolls, cut another thousand aged and weak troops, and memorialized that the reserve battalions be abolished and their men folded into the three great camps; military administration was thereby brought into order on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 倉場總督南居益言：「京營歲支米百六十六萬四千余石，視萬歷四十六年增五萬七千余石，宜減省。」

translations.literal: The granary-field grand coordinator Nan Juyi said: "The capital garrison yearly disburses more than 1,664,000 shi of grain, an increase of more than 57,000 shi over the forty-sixth year of Wanli; it should be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Juyi, Grand Coordinator of the granary fields, reported: "The capital garrison now consumes more than 1,664,000 shi of grain yearly—57,000 shi more than in the forty-sixth year of Wanli—and the amount ought to be cut.

sentences.zh: 邦華因上議軍以十二萬為額，餉以百四十四萬石為額，歲省二十二萬有奇。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of Nan Juyi's speech; Banghua thereupon submitted a proposal fixing troops at a quota of one hundred twenty thousand and rations at a quota of 1,440,000 shi, saving more than two hundred twenty thousand yearly.
translations.idiomatic: End of Nan Juyi's quoted memorial; Li Banghua then proposed fixing troop strength at one hundred twenty thousand and grain rations at 1,440,000 shi, saving more than two hundred twenty thousand shi each year.

sentences.zh: 帝亦報可，著為令。

translations.literal: The emperor also replied assent and established it as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal and made it permanent law.

sentences.zh: 帝知邦華忠，奏無不從，邦華亦感帝知，不顧後患。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Banghua was loyal; no memorial went unheeded, and Banghua also felt the emperor's trust and did not heed later troubles.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Li Banghua to be loyal and approved every proposal he submitted; Li Banghua, moved by this trust, pressed on without regard for the consequences.

sentences.zh: 諸失利者銜次骨，而怨謗紛然矣。

translations.literal: Those who lost advantage harbored hatred to the marrow, and resentful slander arose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had lost their illicit gains hated him to the bone, and calumny spread on every side.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，畿輔被兵，簡精卒三千守通州，二千援薊州，自督諸軍營城外，軍容甚壯。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month the capital region suffered military attack; he selected three thousand crack troops to guard Tongzhou and two thousand to reinforce Jizhou, personally directing all armies camped outside the walls—the army's bearing was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: That October the capital region came under attack; he picked three thousand elite troops to hold Tongzhou and two thousand to reinforce Jizhou, personally directing the armies encamped outside the walls, and the force presented an imposing front.

sentences.zh: 俄有命邦華軍撤還守陴，於是偵者不敢遠出，聲息遂斷，則請防寇賊，緝間諜，散奸宄，禁訛言。

translations.literal: Shortly an order came that Banghua's army withdraw back to guard the battlements; thereupon scouts dared not go far out, intelligence ceased, and he then requested defense against bandits, arrest of spies, dispersal of evil agents, and prohibition of rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an order came for his troops to fall back and man the walls instead; scouts no longer dared venture far, intelligence dried up, and he memorialized for measures against raiders, the arrest of spies, the dispersal of subversives, and a ban on rumor-mongering.

sentences.zh: 邦華自聞警，衣不解帶，捐貲造炮車及諸火器，又以外城單薄，自請出守。

translations.literal: From the time Banghua heard the alarm he did not ungird his belt, donated funds to build gun carriages and various fire weapons, and because the outer wall was thin requested in person to go out and defend.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment the alarm sounded Li Banghua slept in his clothes, spent his own funds to build gun carriages and other firearms, and because the outer walls were weak volunteered to take command outside the city.

sentences.zh: 而諸不逞之徒，乃構蜚語入大內。

translations.literal: Yet various unruly persons thereupon fabricated flying rumors into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet scheming men fabricated slanders and carried them into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 襄城伯李守锜督京營，亦銜邦華扼己，乘間詆諆。

translations.literal: Li Shouqi, Marquis of Xiangcheng, supervised the capital garrison and also resented Banghua for restraining him; seizing an opening he slandered and defamed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouqi, the Marquis of Xiangcheng, who commanded the capital garrison, also resented Li Banghua for curbing his power and seized the chance to denounce him.

sentences.zh: 邦華自危，上疏陳情，歸命於帝。

translations.literal: Banghua felt himself in peril, submitted a memorial stating his feelings, and entrusted his fate to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling himself endangered, Li Banghua submitted a heartfelt memorial and placed his fate entirely in the emperor's hands.

sentences.zh: 會滿桂兵拒大清兵德勝門外，城上發大炮助桂，誤傷桂兵多。

translations.literal: It happened that Man Gui's troops were resisting the Great Qing army outside Desheng Gate; the wall launched great cannon to aid Gui and mistakenly wounded many of Gui's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Man Gui's army was holding the Qing forces outside Desheng Gate; the defenders on the wall fired great guns to support him and accidentally killed many of his own men.

sentences.zh: 都察院都事張道澤遂劾邦華，言官交章論列，遂罷邦華閑住。

translations.literal: Zhang Daoze, director in the Censorate, thereupon impeached Banghua; remonstrating officials submitted memorials in succession, and Banghua was dismissed to idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Daoze, a director in the Censorate, then impeached Li Banghua; censorial officials piled on with memorial after memorial, and he was dismissed to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 自是代者以為戒，率因循姑息，戎政不可問矣。

translations.literal: From then on successors took this as a warning and as a rule followed precedent and indulgence; military administration could no longer be inquired into.
translations.idiomatic: His successors took this as a warning and as a rule shrank into complacency; military administration thereafter sank beyond remedy.

sentences.zh: 邦華前後罷免家居二十年。

translations.literal: Banghua, dismissed and restored before and after, dwelt at home twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Counting his several dismissals and restorations, Li Banghua spent twenty years living at home.

sentences.zh: 父廷諫無恙。

translations.literal: His father Tingjian remained unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout this time his father Li Tingjian remained in good health.

sentences.zh: 十二年四月，起南京兵部尚書，定營制，汰不急之將，並分設之營。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year he was raised as Nanjing Minister of War, fixed camp regulations, cut unneeded generals, and merged separately established camps.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twelfth year of Chongzhen he was recalled as Minister of War at Nanjing, where he reorganized the garrison system, eliminated superfluous officers, and consolidated redundant battalions.

sentences.zh: 謂守江南不若守江北，防下流不若防上流。

translations.literal: He said defending south of the Yangtze was not as good as defending north of it, and guarding the lower reaches was not as good as guarding the upper reaches.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that defending the south bank of the Yangtze was inferior to holding the north bank, and that guarding the lower river was inferior to securing the upper reaches.

sentences.zh: 乃由浦口歷滁、全椒、和，相形勢，繪圖以獻。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Pukou he passed through Chu, Quanjiao, and He, surveyed the terrain, and presented maps.
translations.idiomatic: He then traveled from Pukou through Chu, Quanjiao, and He, surveyed the terrain, and submitted maps of his findings to the throne.

sentences.zh: 於浦口置沿江敵臺，於滁設戍卒，於池河建城垣，於滁、椒咽喉則築堡於藕塘。

translations.literal: At Pukou he placed enemy-facing towers along the river; at Chu he stationed garrison troops; at the Chi River he built city walls; at the throat of Chu and Jiao he built a fort at Outang.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed enemy-watch towers along the river at Pukou, garrison troops at Chu, walls along the Chi River, and a fort at Outang commanding the strategic junction between Chu and Jiao.

sentences.zh: 和遭屠戮，請以隸之太平。

translations.literal: He had suffered massacre; he requested that it be placed under Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: The district of He had suffered slaughter; he asked that it be placed under the jurisdiction of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 又請開府采石之山，置哨太平之港，大墾當塗閑田數萬頃資軍儲。

translations.literal: He also requested opening offices at the hills of Caishi, placing outposts at the harbor of Taiping, and greatly reclaiming tens of thousands of qing of idle fields at Dangtu to fund military stores.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed establishing a command at the Caishi hills, posting sentries at Taiping harbor, and reclaiming tens of thousands of qing of idle land at Dangtu to build up military grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 徐州，南北要害，水陸交會，請宿重兵，設總督，片檄征調，奠陵京萬全之勢。

translations.literal: Xuzhou was the strategic point between north and south, where land and water routes met; he requested stationing heavy troops, establishing a grand coordinator, and that a single dispatch could mobilize forces to secure the imperial tombs and capital in an unassailable posture.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou, the strategic hinge between north and south where land and water routes converged, ought in his view to hold a heavy garrison under a grand coordinator so that a single order could mobilize troops and secure both the imperial tombs and the southern capital beyond challenge.

sentences.zh: 皆下所司，未及行，以父憂去。

translations.literal: All were sent down to the responsible offices; before they could be carried out, he left on account of his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: All these proposals were referred to the relevant offices, but before any could be implemented he resigned to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，起故官，掌南京都察院事，俄代劉宗周為左都御史。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year he was raised to his former office, took charge of Nanjing Censorate affairs, and shortly replaced Liu Zongzhou as Left Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year he was recalled to his former rank, placed in charge of the Nanjing Censorate, and soon succeeded Liu Zongzhou as Left Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 都城被兵，即日請督東南援兵入衛，力疾上道。

translations.literal: When the capital suffered military attack, that very day he requested to direct southeastern relief troops to enter and guard, and forced his illness to take the road.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital came under attack he that same day petitioned to lead southeastern relief forces to its defense and set out at once despite his illness.

sentences.zh: 明年三月抵九江。

translations.literal: The next year in the third month he reached Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The following March he reached Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 左良玉潰兵數十萬，聲言餉乏，欲寄帑於南京，艨艟蔽江東下。

translations.literal: Zuo Liangyu's routed troops numbered several hundred thousand; they proclaimed rations were short and wished to deposit the treasury at Nanjing; war vessels covered the river going east down.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu's shattered army of several hundred thousand men was advancing downriver, claiming their pay was exhausted and demanding that the Nanjing treasury take charge of their funds, while their warships blackened the Yangtze from bank to bank.

sentences.zh: 留都士民一夕數徙，文武大吏相顧愕眙。

translations.literal: The retained capital's gentry and commoners moved several times in a single night; civil and military high officials looked at one another in stunned silence.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Nanjing fled their homes repeatedly in a single night, while civil and military officials stared at one another in helpless dismay.

sentences.zh: 邦華嘆曰：「中原安靜土，東南一角耳。

translations.literal: Banghua sighed and said: "The Central Plain is still quiet land; the southeast is but a corner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua sighed and said: "The Central Plain is still at peace; the southeast is only a corner of the realm.

sentences.zh: 身為大臣，忍坐視決裂，袖手局外而去乎！」

translations.literal: As a great minister, how can I bear to sit and watch the realm tear apart, fold my arms and stand outside the affair, and leave!"
translations.idiomatic: As a senior minister, how could I sit by while the realm tore itself apart, arms folded on the sidelines, and simply walk away?

sentences.zh: 乃停舟草檄告良玉，責以大義。

translations.literal: He then halted his boat, drafted a proclamation in writing to inform Liangyu, and rebuked him with the great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: With that he anchored his boat, drafted a public letter to Zuo Liangyu, and rebuked him in the name of duty to the state.

sentences.zh: 良玉氣沮，答書語頗恭。

translations.literal: Liangyu's spirit was dejected; his reply letter's words were quite respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu's pride was broken; his written reply was notably deferential.

sentences.zh: 邦華用便宜發九江庫銀十五萬餉之，而身入其軍，開誠慰勞。

translations.literal: Banghua, using expedient authority, issued one hundred fifty thousand taels of silver from the Jiujiang treasury to supply them, while himself entering his army, opening his heart in consolation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua exercised emergency powers to release 150,000 taels from the Jiujiang treasury for their pay, then went in person among the troops, speaking frankly to reassure and encourage them.

sentences.zh: 良玉及其下皆感激，誓殺賊報國，一軍遂安。

translations.literal: Liangyu and all under him were grateful; they swore to kill bandits and repay the state, and the whole army was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu and his men were deeply moved; they pledged to kill the rebels in the state's service, and the entire army was settled.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，大喜，陛見嘉勞。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of it and was greatly pleased; he granted an audience at the palace steps and praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he was delighted and summoned Li Banghua to court, where he praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 邦華跪奏移時，數詔起立，溫語如家人，中官屏息遠伏。

translations.literal: Banghua knelt and memorialized for a long while; repeatedly an edict ordered him to rise; warm words like family; palace eunuchs held their breath and crouched far away.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua knelt and spoke at length; several times the emperor ordered him to rise, speaking to him with familial warmth while the eunuchs held their breath and kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 其後召對百官，帝輒目註邦華雲。

translations.literal: Thereafter when summoning officials for audience, the Emperor always fixed his gaze on Banghua.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever he convened the officials, the emperor's eyes always found Li Banghua.

sentences.zh: 舊例，御史出巡，回道考核。

translations.literal: By old precedent, when censorial investigators went on inspection tours, on their return they were assessed on their route.
translations.idiomatic: Under longstanding practice, touring censors were evaluated only after they completed their circuits and returned.

sentences.zh: 邦華謂回道而後黜，害政已多。

translations.literal: Banghua said that waiting until return from the circuit before dismissal already harmed government in many ways.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua argued that waiting until a censor came back to remove him did the realm great harm.

sentences.zh: 論罷巡按、巡鹽御史各一人。

translations.literal: He discussed dismissing one circuit intendant and one salt-circuit censor each.
translations.idiomatic: He secured the dismissal of one touring intendant and one salt-region censor.

sentences.zh: 奉命考試御史，黜冒濫者一人，追黜御史無顯過而先任推官著貪聲者一人。

translations.literal: Ordered to examine censorial investigators, he dismissed one who was presumptuous and excessive, and in retroactive dismissal removed one censor without obvious fault who in an earlier post as investigating censor had a reputation for greed.
translations.idiomatic: In a mandated review of the censorate he removed one unqualified appointee and retroactively dismissed one censor who had no glaring offense on record but had earned a reputation for corruption as a magistrate before promotion.

sentences.zh: 臺中始畏法。

translations.literal: Within the Censorate they first feared the law.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time the censorate took the law seriously.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月，李自成陷山西。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year, Li Zicheng captured Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year of Chongzhen (1644), Li Zicheng overran Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 邦華密疏請帝固守京師，仿永樂朝故事，太子監國南都。

translations.literal: Banghua in a secret memorial asked the Emperor to firmly hold Beijing, following the Yongle reign precedent of the crown prince overseeing the state at the southern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua sent a secret memorial urging the emperor to hold Beijing while following the Yongle precedent of sending the crown prince to Nanjing as regent of the south.

sentences.zh: 居數日未得命，又請定、永二王分封太平、寧國二府，拱護兩京。

translations.literal: After several days without receiving orders, he again asked that the Ding and Yong princes be enfeoffed at the Taiping and Ningguo estates respectively, to flank and protect the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: After several days without a reply he proposed enfeoffing the Princes of Ding and Yong at Taiping and Ningguo to guard the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 帝得疏意動，繞殿行，且讀且嘆，將行其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor, on receiving the memorial, was moved in mind; he walked around the hall, reading and sighing, about to carry out his words.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the memorial, the emperor paced the hall, reading and sighing, on the verge of accepting the plan.

sentences.zh: 會帝召對群臣，中允李明睿疏言南遷便，給事中光時亨以倡言泄密糾之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Emperor summoned officials for audience; zhongyun Li Mingrui memorialized that southern relocation was convenient; supervising secretary Guang Shihang impeached him for advocating talk and leaking secrets.
translations.idiomatic: At an imperial audience the lecturer Li Mingrui urged relocation to the south; the supervising secretary Guang Shihang attacked him for leaking state secrets by broaching the idea.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「國君死社稷，正也，朕誌定矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The ruler of a state dies with the altars of soil and grain — this is correct; my purpose is fixed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "A true sovereign dies with his altars — that is righteousness. My mind is made up.

sentences.zh: 遂罷邦華策不議。

translations.literal: He then set aside Banghua's plan without discussion.
translations.idiomatic: With that he shelved Li Banghua's proposals without further debate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊逼都城，亟詣內閣言事。

translations.literal: Before long bandits pressed the capital; he urgently went to the Grand Secretariat to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels were at the gates; Li Banghua hurried to the Grand Secretariat to plead for action.

sentences.zh: 魏藻德漫應曰：「姑待之。」

translations.literal: Wei Zaode answered casually: "For now wait."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zaode replied dismissively: "Let us wait a while.

sentences.zh: 邦華太息而出。

translations.literal: Banghua sighed deeply and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Banghua left with a heavy sigh.

sentences.zh: 已，率諸御史登城，群奄拒之不得上。

translations.literal: After this he led the various censors to ascend the wall; a throng of eunuchs blocked them and they could not go up.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his fellow censors to the walls, but eunuchs barred them from ascending.

sentences.zh: 十八日，外城陷，走宿文信國祠。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day the outer city fell; he fled to lodge at the Lord of Wen's Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth the outer city fell; he took refuge in the shrine of the Duke of Wen.

sentences.zh: 明日，內城亦陷，乃三揖信國曰：「邦華死國難，請從先生於九京矣。」

translations.literal: The next day the inner city also fell; he then thrice bowed to Xin Guo and said: "Banghua dies in the state's calamity; I beg to follow the Master to the nine capitals."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the inner city fell as well; he bowed three times to the duke's spirit and said: "Banghua dies for the realm; let me follow you to the grave.

sentences.zh: 為詩曰：「堂堂丈夫兮聖賢為徒，忠孝大節兮誓死靡渝，臨危授命兮吾無愧吾。」

translations.literal: He made a poem saying: "Upright great husband — the sages and worthies are my fellows; great integrity of loyalty and filial piety — sworn unto death without change; facing peril and receiving mandate — I have no shame before myself."
translations.idiomatic: He composed a poem: "A true man takes the sages as his companions; loyalty and filial piety are vows I will not break even in death; facing peril I accept my fate — I have no shame before myself.

sentences.zh: 遂投繯而絕。

translations.literal: He then cast himself on a cord and ended.
translations.idiomatic: With that he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 贈太保、吏部尚書，謚忠文。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted Grand Mentor and Minister of Personnel; posthumous title Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Mentor and Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Zhongwen (Loyal and Literary).

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚忠肅。

translations.literal: This dynasty bestowed posthumous title Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty granted the posthumous title Zhongsu (Loyal and Reverent).

sentences.zh: 王家彥，字開美，莆田人。

translations.literal: Wang Jiayan, style name Kaimei, a man of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiayan (style Kaimei) was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Tianqi (1622).

sentences.zh: 授開化知縣，調蘭溪。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Kaihua; transferred to Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Kaihua and later transferred to Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 擢刑科給事中，彈擊權貴無所避。

translations.literal: Promoted to supervising secretary of the Penal Branch; he attacked powerful and noble without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to supervising secretary in the Penal Branch, he impeached the powerful without fear.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，請釋大學士錢龍錫於獄，龍錫得減死。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he asked to release Grand Secretary Qian Longxi from prison; Longxi received commutation from death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen (1631) he pleaded for the release of Grand Secretary Qian Longxi from prison; Qian was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 請推行按月奏報例於四方，獄囚得無久淹。

translations.literal: He asked to extend the monthly report precedent to all quarters; prisoners in jail could avoid long detention.
translations.idiomatic: He urged extending monthly judicial reporting throughout the empire so prisoners would not languish in jail.

sentences.zh: 閩海盜劉香擾郡邑，撫鎮追剿多失利，朝議召募，將大舉。

translations.literal: Fujian sea pirate Liu Xiang harassed commanderies and districts; the governor and regional commander in pursuit and suppression mostly met with losses; court discussion was to recruit troops and launch a major campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The pirate Liu Xiang ravaged the Fujian coast; provincial and military commanders suffered repeated defeats, and the court prepared a major recruitment drive.

sentences.zh: 家彥言：「舊制，衛所軍餼於官，無別兵亦無別將，統於各衛之指揮。

translations.literal: Jiayan said: "The old system: guard and battalion soldiers were fed by the state, with no separate troops and no separate generals; all were commanded under each guard's director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiayan argued: "Under the old system guard troops were state-provisioned, with no separate armies or generals; they answered to their guard commanders.

sentences.zh: 寨設號船，聊絡呼應，又添設遊擊等官，雖支洋窮港，戈船相望。

translations.literal: Stockades set signal boats for slight liaison and response; moreover they added roving-patrol officers and such; though they reached foreign seas and remote harbors, dagger-axe boats faced one another in sight.
translations.idiomatic: Signal ships linked the coastal posts, and roaming-patrol officers were added layer upon layer, yet though their warships crowded every inlet, they only lined the coast without real coordination.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以今日策防海，莫若復舊制，勤訓練。

translations.literal: Your servant in foolishness considers that for today's coastal defense, nothing is better than restoring the old system and diligently training.
translations.idiomatic: I believe coastal defense today is best served by restoring that system and training the troops properly.

sentences.zh: 練則衛所軍皆勁卒，不練雖添設召募兵，猶驅市人而戰之，糜餉擾民無益，賊終不能盡。」

translations.literal: With training then guard and battalion soldiers are all crack troops; without training, though you add recruited troops, it is still driving market folk to battle — wasting rations, troubling the people without benefit; bandits in the end cannot be exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Trained guard troops become real soldiers; without training, recruited levies are merely market crowds pressed into battle — wasting pay, burdening the people, and never destroying the pirates.

sentences.zh: 時以為名言。

translations.literal: At the time it was regarded as famous words.
translations.idiomatic: The remark was hailed as wisdom.

sentences.zh: 奉命巡青，所條奏多議行。

translations.literal: Ordered to inspect Qing, his listed memorials mostly were discussed and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: On an inspection tour of Shandong he submitted many proposals, most of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 先是，隆慶間太仆種馬額存十二萬五千，邊馬至二十六萬。

translations.literal: Earlier, between the Longqing reign the Court of Imperial Horses' breeding-horse quota retained one hundred twenty-five thousand; border horses reached two hundred sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Longqing era the stud farms had 125,000 breeding horses on the rolls and border herds reached 260,000.

sentences.zh: 言者以民間最苦養馬，所納馬又不足用，議馬征銀十兩，加草料銀二兩，歲可得銀百四十四萬兩。

translations.literal: Speakers said the people suffered most from raising horses; the horses delivered were also insufficient for use; they proposed horse levy of ten taels of silver, plus forage silver two taels, annually obtaining one million four hundred forty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Critics noted that raising horses imposed the heaviest burden on households and the animals supplied were poor; they proposed a commutation fee of ten taels per horse plus two taels for fodder, yielding 1.44 million taels a year.

sentences.zh: 中樞楊博持不可，詔折其半，而馬政始變。

translations.literal: Minister of the Center Yang Bo held it could not be done; an edict halved it, and horse administration then changed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Bo resisted; the court halved the fee, and the horse policy began to change.

sentences.zh: 萬歷九年議盡行改折，南寺歲征銀二十二萬，北寺五十一萬，銀入冏寺而馬政日弛。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wanli they discussed fully converting to silver commutation; the southern stud farm annually levied two hundred twenty thousand taels, the northern five hundred ten thousand; silver entered the Court of Imperial Horses while horse administration daily slackened.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 9 (1581) full commutation was adopted: the southern stud farm collected 220,000 taels a year, the northern 510,000; cash flowed in but the herds deteriorated daily.

sentences.zh: 家彥極陳其弊，請改國初種馬及西番茶馬之制。

translations.literal: Jiayan extremely set forth its harms, asking to restore the founding-era breeding-horse system and the Western Tribes tea-horse system.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiayan detailed the harm and urged restoring the early-Ming stud system and the tea-for-horses trade with Tibet.

sentences.zh: 又班軍舊額十六萬，後減至七萬，至是止二萬有奇，更有建議盡征行糧、月糧，免其番上者。

translations.literal: Also rotational troops' old quota was one hundred sixty thousand; later reduced to seventy thousand; by this time only a little over twenty thousand; moreover there were proposals to fully levy campaign grain and monthly grain, exempting them from rotational duty at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Rotational troops had fallen from a nominal 160,000 to 70,000 and now barely 20,000; some proposed replacing all grain allotments with cash and exempting them from capital duty entirely.

sentences.zh: 家彥時巡京營，力陳不可，且請免其工役，盡歸行伍。

translations.literal: Jiayan at the time inspecting the Capital Garrison, forcefully set forth it could not be done, and moreover asked to free them from corvée labor, fully returning them to the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the capital garrison he argued firmly against the plan and asked that corvée duties be lifted so the men could return to full service.

sentences.zh: 帝皆褒納其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor all praised and accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and adopted all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 遵化鐵冶久廢，奸民請開之，家彥言有害無利。

translations.literal: Zunhua iron smelting had long been abandoned; wicked commoners asked to open it; Jiayan said there was harm without profit.
translations.idiomatic: The Zunhua ironworks had long been shut; speculators sought to reopen them, but Wang Jiayan showed the project would harm the realm without profit.

sentences.zh: 復有請開開化雲霧山以興屯者，亦以家彥言而止。

translations.literal: Again there were those who asked to open Kaihua's Yunwu Mountain to promote garrison farming; this too was stopped on Jiayan's words.
translations.idiomatic: A proposal to open Yunwu Mountain in Kaihua for military colonies was likewise blocked on his advice.

sentences.zh: 屢遷戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: Repeatedly transferred to chief supervising secretary of the Revenue Branch.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted, becoming chief supervising secretary of the Revenue Branch.

sentences.zh: 軍興餉詘，總督盧象升有因糧加餉之議，戶部尚書侯恂請於未被寇之地，士大夫家賦銀兩者，加二錢；

translations.literal: With military campaigns rising, provisions were short; Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng had a proposal to add to provisions based on grain tax; Minister of Revenue Hou Xun asked that in places not yet ravaged by bandits, scholar-official households assessed one tael of silver, add two cash;
translations.idiomatic: War funds ran short; Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng proposed surcharges on grain tax; Revenue Minister Hou Xun suggested that in unscathed regions scholar-official households taxed one tael should pay an extra 2 cash;

sentences.zh: 民間五兩以上者，兩加一錢。

translations.literal: among the common people those of five taels and above, per tael add one cash.
translations.idiomatic: and common households assessed five taels or more should pay an extra cash per tael.

sentences.zh: 家彥言：「民賦五兩上者，率百十家成一戶，非富民，不可以朘削。」

translations.literal: Jiayan said: "For people's assessments of five taels and above, on average a hundred or more households make one household; they are not rich households; they cannot be pared down."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiayan objected: "Households assessed at five taels or more usually represent a hundred poor families grouped as one tax unit — not the wealthy — and must not be squeezed further.

sentences.zh: 軍食不足，畿輔、山東、河南、江北召買米豆輸天津，至九十余萬石，吏胥侵耗率數十萬。

translations.literal: Army provisions were insufficient; the metropolitan region, Shandong, Henan, and Jiangbei requisitioned purchase of rice and beans transported to Tianjin, reaching more than nine hundred thousand shi; clerks and runners embezzled and wasted on average several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With army rations short, the government requisitioned over 900,000 shi of grain and beans from the capital region, Shandong, Henan, and northern Jiangsu for Tianjin; clerks skimmed tens of thousands of shi.

sentences.zh: 家彥請嚴治，帝並采納焉。

translations.literal: Jiayan asked for strict punishment; the Emperor adopted all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiayan demanded severe punishment for the theft; the emperor accepted both proposals.

sentences.zh: 憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 十二年起吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he rose to chief supervising secretary of the Personnel Branch.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Chongzhen he returned as chief supervising secretary of the Personnel Branch.

sentences.zh: 流寇日熾，緣墨吏朘民，民益走為盜。

translations.literal: Roaming bandits daily grew fierce, because corrupt clerks pared the people; the people increasingly fled to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry grew daily because corrupt officials squeezed the people, who fled into outlawry.

sentences.zh: 盜日多，民生日蹙。

translations.literal: Bandits daily increased; people's lives daily grew tight.
translations.idiomatic: As outlaws multiplied, common life grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 家彥上疏曰：「臣見秦、晉之間，饑民相煽，千百為群。

translations.literal: Jiayan submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant sees that between Qin and Jin, starving people incite one another, gathering in groups of hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiayan memorialized: "I see across Shaanxi and Shanxi starving people stirring one another into bands of hundreds and thousands.

sentences.zh: 其始率自一鄉一邑，守令早為之所，取《周官荒政十二》而行之，民何至接踵為盜，盜何至潰裂以極？

translations.literal: At first they generally came from one village or one district; if the prefect and magistrate early took measures, taking the Zhou Offices' Twelve Famine Policies and implementing them, how would the people come to join as bandits one after another, how would bandits reach the extreme of bursting apart?
translations.idiomatic: At first it is a village or a county; if local officials acted early under the Zhou famine relief statutes, how would people turn to banditry in droves, and how would outlawry spiral out of control?

sentences.zh: 論者謂功令使然，催科急者書上考，督責嚴者號循良，不肖而墨者以束濕濟其饕餮，一二賢明吏束於文法，展布莫由。

translations.literal: Discussants say examination regulations make it so: those urgent in tax collection get written as top grade; those strict in supervision and blame are called orderly and good; the unworthy and corrupt use wet rope to satisfy their gluttony; one or two worthy and enlightened officials are bound by statutes, with no way to unfold their policies.
translations.idiomatic: Critics blame the examination system: officials who press tax collection hardest earn top ratings; the harshest enforcers are called model governors; the corrupt wring what they can from the people while a few honest magistrates are trapped by regulations and cannot govern freely.

sentences.zh: 惟稍寬文網，壹令撫綏，盜之聚者可散，散者可不復聚。

translations.literal: Only if slightly loosening the net of statutes, unifying orders to soothe and settle, those gathered as bandits can be dispersed, those dispersed can fail to gather again.
translations.idiomatic: Only by loosening legal strictures and giving local officials a single mandate to pacify the countryside can gathered rebels be dispersed and stay dispersed.

sentences.zh: 又舊制捕蝗令，吏部歲九月頒勘合於有司，請實意舉行。」

translations.literal: Moreover the old system locust-catching decree: the Ministry of Personnel every ninth month issued verification tallies to local officials; he asked to earnestly carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged enforcing the old locust-control regulations, which the Ministry of Personnel issued each ninth month — and asked that officials carry them out in earnest.

sentences.zh: 帝皆納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor adopted all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of it.

sentences.zh: 擢大理丞，進本寺少卿。

translations.literal: Promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review; advanced to vice minister of that court.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director and then vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十五年遷太仆卿。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1642) he became Director of the Court of Imperial Horses.

sentences.zh: 家彥向言馬政，帝下兵部檄陜西督撫，未能行。

translations.literal: Jiayan had earlier spoken on horse administration; the Emperor sent down the Ministry of War's dispatch to Shaanxi governor and coordinator, but it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He had long urged horse-policy reform; the emperor ordered the Ministry of War to instruct Shaanxi authorities, but nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 至是，四疏言馬耗之故，請行官牧及金牌差發遺制。

translations.literal: At this time, in four memorials he set forth the causes of horse depletion, asking to implement government pasturage and the old system of golden-plaque requisition dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Now he sent four memorials on the collapse of the herds, urging restoration of state stud farms and the old golden-plaque requisition system.

sentences.zh: 且言：「課馬改折，舊增至二十四萬兩，已重困。

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "Horse-tax commutation to silver, originally increased to two hundred forty thousand taels, already heavily distressed.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Commutation for horse tax had already risen to 240,000 taels and badly burdened the people.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌不恤民，復增三十七萬，致舊額反逋，不可不厘正。」

translations.literal: Yang Sichang without pity for the people again added three hundred seventy thousand, causing the old quota in turn to fall into arrears; this cannot but be rectified."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang, heedless of the people's plight, added another 370,000 taels, leaving even the old levy in arrears — this must be corrected.

sentences.zh: 帝手其疏，語執政曰：「家彥奏皆善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor held his memorial in hand and told the chief ministers: "All of Jiayan's memorials are good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held the memorials and told his ministers: "Everything Wang Jiayan proposes is sound.

sentences.zh: 敕議行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered discussion and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them debated and implemented.

sentences.zh: 然軍興方亟，不能盡舉也。

translations.literal: Yet with military campaigns just urgent, it could not all be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: But the exigencies of war prevented full implementation.

sentences.zh: 頃之，擢戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly after, promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 都城被兵，命協理戎政。

translations.literal: The capital was subjected to military attack; he was ordered to assist in managing martial administration.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital came under siege he was ordered to assist in military administration.

sentences.zh: 即日登陴，閱視內外城十六門。

translations.literal: That very day he ascended the ramparts, inspecting the inner and outer city's sixteen gates.
translations.idiomatic: The same day he climbed the walls and inspected all sixteen gates of the inner and outer city.

sentences.zh: 雪夜，攜一燈，步巡城堞，人無知者。

translations.literal: On a snowy night, carrying one lamp, he walked inspecting the battlements; no one knew him.
translations.idiomatic: One snowy night he walked the battlements alone with a single lamp, unrecognized by anyone.

sentences.zh: 翊日校勤惰，將士皆服，爭自勵。

translations.literal: The next day he checked diligence and sloth; officers and soldiers all submitted, striving to encourage themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he reviewed diligence and slackness; the troops were impressed and strove to improve.

sentences.zh: 初，分守阜成門，後移安定門，寢處城樓者半歲。

translations.literal: At first he was assigned to guard Fucheng Gate; later transferred to Anding Gate; he slept in the gate tower for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: He first guarded Fucheng Gate, then Anding Gate, sleeping in the gate tower for half a year.

sentences.zh: 解嚴，賜宴午門，增秩一等。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, he was given a banquet at the Meridian Gate and one rank added.
translations.idiomatic: When the emergency passed he was feasted at the Meridian Gate and given one rank of promotion.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月，廷推戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year, court recommendation for Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year (1644) the court recommended him for Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「戎政非家彥不可。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Martial administration cannot do without Jiayan."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Military affairs cannot do without Wang Jiayan.

sentences.zh: 特留任。

translations.literal: He was specially kept in his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially kept in his post.

sentences.zh: 賊逼京師，襄城伯李國禎督京營，又命中官王德化盡督內外軍。

translations.literal: Bandits pressed the capital; Xiangcheng Earl Li Guozhen supervised the Capital Garrison; again the Emperor ordered eunuch Wang Dehua fully to supervise inner and outer armies.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels neared the capital, Earl Li Guozhen of Xiangcheng commanded the capital garrison while eunuch Wang Dehua was given overall command of all forces.

sentences.zh: 國禎發三大營軍城外，守陴益少。

translations.literal: Guozhen dispatched the three great battalions' troops outside the city; defenders on the parapets grew ever fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guozhen sent the Three Great Camps outside the walls, leaving ever fewer men on the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 諸軍既出城，見賊輒降，降卒反攻城，城上人皆其儕，益無固誌。

translations.literal: Once the various troops left the city, meeting bandits they immediately surrendered; surrendered troops in turn attacked the city; those on the wall were all their mates; increasingly there was no firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Once outside, the soldiers surrendered at sight of the enemy; the surrendered men then turned back to storm the walls, and the defenders recognized them as comrades — morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 廷臣分門守，家彥守安定門。

translations.literal: Court ministers each guarded a gate separately; Jiayan guarded Anding Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials were assigned gates; Wang Jiayan held Anding Gate.

sentences.zh: 號令進止由中官，沮諸臣毋得登城，又縋叛監杜勛上，與密約而去。

translations.literal: Commands to advance and halt were by eunuchs; they obstructed the various ministers from ascending the wall; moreover they lowered the rebel intelligence officer Du Xun up on a rope, with a secret pact, and he left.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs controlled all orders, barred officials from the walls, and lowered the turncoat Du Xun up on a rope to make a secret deal and flee.

sentences.zh: 帝手敕兵部尚書張縉彥登城察視，家彥從，中官猶固拒，示之手敕，問勛安在，曰：「去矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor by hand-edict ordered Minister of War Zhang Jinyan to ascend the wall to inspect; Jiayan followed; eunuchs still stubbornly refused, until shown the hand-edict; asked where Xun was, they said: "Gone."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered War Minister Zhang Jinyan to inspect the walls; Wang Jiayan went with him; the eunuchs still blocked them until shown the imperial order; asked where Du Xun was, they said he had gone.

sentences.zh: 秦、晉二王欲上城，家彥曰：「二王降賊，即賊也。

translations.literal: The Qin and Jin two princes wished to ascend the wall; Jiayan said: "The two princes surrendered to bandits — they are bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the Princes of Qin and Jin tried to come up, Wang Jiayan said: "Those princes have surrendered to the enemy — they are the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊安得上！」

translations.literal: How can bandits be allowed up!"
translations.idiomatic: How dare the enemy be admitted to the walls!

sentences.zh: 頓足哭。

translations.literal: He stamped his foot and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He stamped his feet and wept.

sentences.zh: 偕縉彥詣宮門請見，不得入。

translations.literal: Together with Jinyan he went to the palace gate to request audience, and could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhang Jinyan went to the palace gates to beg an audience but were refused entry.

sentences.zh: 黎明，城陷，家彥投城下，不死，自縊於民舍，遭賊焚，殘其一臂，仆收其余體焉。

translations.literal: At dawn the city fell; Jiayan cast himself below the wall, did not die, hanged himself in a commoner's house; encountering bandits' burning, one arm was left; a servant collected the rest of the body.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the city fell; Wang Jiayan leapt from the wall but survived, then hanged himself in a private house; rebels set the fire that consumed him, leaving one arm; a servant gathered the rest of his body.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保、兵部尚書，謚忠端。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted Crown Prince Grand Tutor and Minister of War; posthumous title Zhongduan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and Minister of War, with the posthumous title Zhongduan (Loyal and Upright).

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚忠毅。

translations.literal: Our dynasty bestowed posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty granted him the posthumous title Zhongyi (Loyal and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 孟兆祥，字允吉，山西澤州人也。

translations.literal: Meng Zhaoxiang, courtesy name Yungji, was a man of Zezhou, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhaoxiang, courtesy name Yungji, came from Zezhou in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 世籍交河，舉於鄉，九赴會試。

translations.literal: For generations his household was registered at Jiaohe; he was successful in the provincial exam, and nine times attended the metropolitan exam.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been registered in Jiaohe for generations; after passing the provincial examination he sat the metropolitan examination nine times.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年始擢第，除大理左評事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was at last promoted to a degree and was appointed Left Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1622 he at last passed the metropolitan examination and was made Assessor on the Left of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，遷吏部稽勛主事，歷文選員外郎。

translations.literal: Early in Chongzhen he was transferred to Supervisor of Records in the Ministry of Personnel, then served as Vice Commissioner in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongzhen reign he became Supervisor of Records in the Ministry of Personnel and later Vice Commissioner in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 門生謁選請善地，兆祥正色拒之，其人悚然退。

translations.literal: A protégé seeking appointment asked for a favorable post; Zhaoxiang sternly refused him, and the man withdrew in dread.
translations.idiomatic: When a protégé came seeking a good appointment, Zhaoxiang rebuffed him with a stern face and the man slunk away.

sentences.zh: 進稽勛郎中，歷考功。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of Records and served in the Bureau of Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of Records and also served in the Bureau of Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 忤權要，貶行人司副，稍遷光祿丞，進少卿。

translations.literal: Having offended powerful figures, he was demoted to Vice Commissioner in the Bureau of Foreign Tributaries, then gradually promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Senior Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Offending the powerful, he was demoted to Vice Commissioner in the Bureau of Foreign Tributaries, but was gradually restored as Vice Director and then Senior Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 歷左通政、太仆卿，旋進通政使，拜刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as Left Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then was soon promoted Commissioner of Transmission and appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left Vice Commissioner of Transmission, Director of the Imperial Stud, and soon became Commissioner of Transmission and Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 賊薄都城，兆祥分守正陽門。

translations.literal: When bandits pressed the capital, Zhaoxiang was assigned to defend Zhengyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: As rebels neared the capital, Zhaoxiang was posted to defend Zhengyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 襄城伯李國禎統京營軍，稽月餉不予，士無固誌。

translations.literal: Earl Li Guozhen of Xiangcheng commanded the capital garrison and withheld monthly pay, so the soldiers lacked firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangcheng Earl Li Guozhen commanded the capital troops but withheld their monthly pay, and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 城陷，兆祥曰：「社稷已覆，吾將安之！」

translations.literal: When the city fell, Zhaoxiang said: "The altars of state are overturned — where shall I go to live!
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he cried: "The realm is destroyed — where can I possibly go on living!

sentences.zh: 自經於門下。

translations.literal: He hanged himself beneath the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He hanged himself under the gate.

sentences.zh: 長子章明，字綱宜，甫成進士，兆祥揮之曰：「我死，汝可去。」

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhang Ming, courtesy name Gangyi, had just passed the jinshi examination; Zhaoxiang waved him away saying: "I am dying — you may leave.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhang Ming, styled Gangyi, had just earned his jinshi degree; Zhaoxiang motioned him away and said: "I am about to die — you should go.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「君父大節也，君亡父死，我何生為！」

translations.literal: He replied: "Loyalty to ruler and father is the great duty; ruler perished and father dead — why should I go on living!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ming answered: "Duty to sovereign and father is the supreme obligation; with the emperor gone and my father dead, why should I still live!"

sentences.zh: 乃投繯於父之側。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cast a noose beside his father.
translations.idiomatic: He then hanged himself beside his father.

sentences.zh: 兆祥妻呂，章明妻王相向哭，既而曰：「彼父子死忠矣，我二人獨不能死乎！」

translations.literal: Zhaoxiang's wife Lü and Zhang Ming's wife Wang faced one another weeping; then they said: "Those father and son have died in loyalty — shall we two alone not die!
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxiang's wife Lü and Zhang Ming's wife Wang wept facing each other, then said: "Father and son have died loyal deaths — are we alone unable to die!

sentences.zh: 皆自縊。

translations.literal: Both hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Both women hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 兆祥贈刑部尚書，謚忠貞，章明河南道御史，謚節湣。

translations.literal: Zhaoxiang was posthumously made Minister of Justice with posthumous title Zhongzhen; Zhang Ming Henan Investigating Censor with posthumous title Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxiang was posthumously made Minister of Justice with the title Zhongzhen; Zhang Ming, Investigating Censor of the Henan Circuit, with the title Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜兆祥謚忠靖，章明貞孝。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted Zhaoxiang posthumous title Zhongjing and Zhang Ming Zhenxiao.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty granted Zhaoxiang the posthumous title Zhongjing and Zhang Ming Zhenxiao.

sentences.zh: 施邦曜，字爾韜，余姚人。

translations.literal: Shi Bangyao, courtesy name Ertao, was a man of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bangyao, courtesy name Ertao, was from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1613.

sentences.zh: 不樂為吏，改順天武學教授，歷國子博士、工部營繕主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: Unhappy in office, he transferred to Instructor at the Shuntian Military School, then served as Lecturer in the Imperial Academy, Principal Secretary in the Bureau of Construction, and rose to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Disliking official life, he became instructor at the Shuntian Military School, then Lecturer at the Imperial Academy, Principal Secretary in the Bureau of Construction, and eventually Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢興三殿工，諸曹郎奔走其門，邦曜不往。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhongxian undertook work on the Three Halls, various bureau directors flocked to his door; Bangyao did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian launched construction on the Three Halls, bureau chiefs crowded his door; Bangyao stayed away.

sentences.zh: 忠賢欲困之，使拆北堂，期五日，適大風拔屋，免譙責。

translations.literal: Zhongxian wanted to trouble him and ordered him to demolish the North Hall within five days; just then a great wind tore up houses, and he was spared reproof.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian tried to trap him by assigning demolition of the North Hall within five days; a great wind that tore up buildings spared him blame.

sentences.zh: 又使作獸吻，仿嘉靖間制，莫考。

translations.literal: Again he was made to fashion ridge beasts after the Jiajing model, which no one could trace.
translations.idiomatic: He was next ordered to make ridge beasts matching the Jiajing design, but no records survived.

sentences.zh: 夢神告之，發地得吻，嘉靖舊物也，忠賢不能難。

translations.literal: A deity told him in a dream; digging the ground he found the beast — an old Jiajing relic — and Zhongxian could not fault him.
translations.idiomatic: A god appeared in his dream; digging he unearthed the beast — an old Jiajing piece — and Zhongxian could not fault him.

sentences.zh: 遷屯田郎中，稍遷漳州知府，盡知屬縣奸盜主名，每發輒得，闔郡驚為神。

translations.literal: Promoted to Director of State Farms, then gradually to Prefect of Zhangzhou; he knew by name every rogue chief in the subordinate counties, and whenever he moved they were caught — the whole prefecture marveled as at a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Director of State Farms and later Prefect of Zhangzhou, he knew every bandit chief by name in his counties; each raid captured its quarry, and the prefecture hailed him as uncanny.

sentences.zh: 盜劉香、李魁奇橫海上，邦曜縶香母誘之，香就擒。

translations.literal: The pirates Liu Xiang and Li Kuiki dominated the sea; Bangyao seized Xiang's mother to lure him, and Xiang surrendered and was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates Liu Xiang and Li Kuiki terrorized the coast; Bangyao detained Xiang's mother as bait, and Xiang came in and was captured.

sentences.zh: 魁奇援鄭芝龍事請撫，邦曜言於巡撫鄒維璉討平之。

translations.literal: Kuiki invoked Zheng Zhilong's case to seek pacification; Bangyao advised Grand Coordinator Zou Weilian to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Kuiki cited Zheng Zhilong's precedent to request enfeoffment; Bangyao urged Grand Coordinator Zou Weilian to pacify and crush him.

sentences.zh: 遷福建副使、左參政、四川按察使、福建左布政使，並有聲。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Fujian Vice Commissioner, Left Administrator, Sichuan Surveillance Commissioner, and Fujian Left Provincial Commissioner — everywhere gaining renown.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Fujian Vice Commissioner, Left Administrator, Sichuan Surveillance Commissioner, and Fujian Left Provincial Commissioner, earning acclaim everywhere.

sentences.zh: 或饋之朱墨竹者，姊子在旁請受之。

translations.literal: Someone presented him with red-ink bamboo paintings; his wife's nephew at his side asked to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: When someone offered him paintings in red ink on bamboo, his wife's nephew beside him asked to accept.

sentences.zh: 曰：「不可。

translations.literal: He said: "It is not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "That will not do.

sentences.zh: 我受之，即彼得以乘間而嘗我，我則示之以可欲之門矣。」

translations.literal: If I accept, then they can seize an opening to try me — I would be showing them the gate of desire.
translations.idiomatic: If I take it, they will find a crack through which to tempt me; I would be showing them where desire may enter.

sentences.zh: 性好山水。

translations.literal: His nature loved mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: He loved landscape scenery by nature.

sentences.zh: 或勸之遊峨嵋，曰：「上官遊覽，動煩屬吏支應，傷小民幾許物力矣。」

translations.literal: Some urged him to tour Mount Emei; he said: "When superiors travel for pleasure, it often burdens subordinate officials with support — how much of the people's goods is wasted!
translations.idiomatic: Urged to visit Mount Emei, he said: "When superiors go sightseeing, subordinates must supply them — how much of the people's wealth is squandered!

sentences.zh: 其潔己愛民如此。

translations.literal: Such was his purity and love for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the way he kept himself pure and cherished the people.

sentences.zh: 歷兩京光祿寺卿，改通政使。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments in both capitals, then was made Commissioner of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments in both capitals, then became Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 黃道周既謫官，復逮下詔獄。

translations.literal: After Huang Daozhou was demoted, he was again seized and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Daozhou's demotion he was again arrested and thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 國子生塗仲吉上書訟之，邦曜不為封進，而大署其副封曰：「書不必上，論不可不存。」

translations.literal: A National University student Tu Zhongji memorialized in his defense; Bangyao did not forward-seal it, but wrote boldly on the duplicate cover: "The memorial need not go up; the argument must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: National University student Tu Zhongji petitioned in Huang's defense; Bangyao did not seal and forward it but wrote large on the duplicate: "The petition need not reach the throne, but the argument must not be silenced.

sentences.zh: 仲吉劾邦曜，邦曜以副封上。

translations.literal: Zhongji impeached Bangyao; Bangyao submitted the duplicate cover.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji impeached Bangyao, who then submitted the duplicate itself.

sentences.zh: 帝見其署語，怒，下仲吉獄，而奪邦曜官。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw the inscription and grew angry, threw Zhongji into prison, and stripped Bangyao of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw what he had written, imprisoned Zhongji, and dismissed Bangyao.

sentences.zh: 逾年起南京通政使。

translations.literal: More than a year later he was appointed Commissioner of Transmission at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed Nanjing Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 入都陛見，陳學術、吏治、用兵、財賦四事，帝改容納焉。

translations.literal: Entering the capital for audience, he presented four topics — learning, officialdom, military use, and revenue — and the Emperor's expression changed as he accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: At audience in the capital he laid out four topics — scholarship, administration, warfare, and finance — and the emperor received them with changed expression.

sentences.zh: 出都三日，命中使召還，曰：「南京無事，留此為朕效力。」

translations.literal: Three days out of the capital an imperial messenger recalled him, saying: "Nanjing has no urgent business; remain here and serve Us.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after leaving, an imperial messenger recalled him: "Nanjing has nothing pressing — stay and serve Us here.

sentences.zh: 吏部推刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel recommended him as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel recommended him for Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「邦曜清執，可左副都御史。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Bangyao's integrity is firm — he may be Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Bangyao is upright and resolute; he may be made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時崇禎十六年十二月也。

translations.literal: It was the twelfth month of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: This was December of Chongzhen 16 (January 1644).

sentences.zh: 明年，賊薄近郊。

translations.literal: The next year bandits pressed the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year rebels neared the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 邦曜語兵部尚書張縉彥檄天下兵勤王，縉彥慢弗省，邦曜太息而去。

translations.literal: Bangyao told Minister of War Zhang Jinyan to issue a dispatch mobilizing troops throughout the realm to rescue the throne; Jinyan was lax and paid no heed; Bangyao sighed and left.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyao urged War Minister Zhang Jinyan to mobilize forces empire-wide; Jinyan was indifferent; Bangyao sighed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 城陷，趨長安門，聞帝崩，慟哭曰：「君殉社稷矣，臣子可偷生哉！」

translations.literal: When the city fell he hastened to Chang'an Gate; hearing the Emperor had perished, he wailed: "The sovereign has died for the altars — how can a subject cling to life!
translations.idiomatic: At the city's fall he rushed to Chang'an Gate; learning of the emperor's death he wept: "The ruler has perished for the state — how can a minister steal life!

sentences.zh: 即解帶自經。

translations.literal: He loosened his belt and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He undid his belt and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 仆救之蘇，恨曰：「是兒誤我！」

translations.literal: Servants revived him; he said angrily: "This boy has ruined me!
translations.idiomatic: Servants revived him; he exclaimed in anger: "This boy has ruined me!

sentences.zh: 賊滿衢巷，不得還邸舍，望門求縊，輒為居民所麾。

translations.literal: Bandits filled the lanes and he could not return to his residence; he looked from door to door for a place to hang himself and was driven off by residents.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels thronged the streets; unable to reach home he begged at door after door for a place to hang himself and was turned away.

sentences.zh: 乃命家人市信石雜澆酒，即途中服之，血迸裂而卒。

translations.literal: He ordered his household to buy arsenic mixed in wine and drank it on the road; blood burst forth and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He had servants buy arsenic mixed with wine and drank it in the street; blood burst from him and he died.

sentences.zh: 邦曜少好王守仁之學，以理學、文章、經濟三分其書而讀之，慕義無窮。

translations.literal: From youth Bangyao loved the learning of Wang Shouren; he divided his books into three parts — Neo-Confucian principle, literary composition, and statecraft — and read them, cherishing righteousness without end.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he admired Wang Yangming, dividing his reading into Neo-Confucian philosophy, letters, and statecraft, and pursued righteousness without limit.

sentences.zh: 魯時生者，裏同年生也，官庶吉士，歿京師。

translations.literal: Lu Shisheng, a fellow townsman and examination-year mate, served as Hanlin Bachelor and died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shisheng, a fellow townsman of the same examination year, was a Hanlin bachelor and died in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 邦曜手治含斂，以女妻其子。

translations.literal: Bangyao personally prepared the encoffining and married his daughter to Lu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyao personally prepared the burial rites and gave his daughter to Lu's son in marriage.

sentences.zh: 嘗買一婢，命灑掃，至東隅，捧篲凝視而泣。

translations.literal: Once he bought a maid and ordered her to sweep; reaching the east corner she held the broom gazing fixedly and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He once bought a maid and set her to sweep; at the eastern corner she held her broom, stared, and wept.

sentences.zh: 怪問之，曰：「此先人御史宅也。

translations.literal: Astonished, he asked her; she said: "This was my late father's residence as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Asked in surprise, she said: "This was my father's house when he was investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時墮環茲地，不覺淒愴耳。」

translations.literal: I fell from the balustrade here at the time — I could not help grieving.
translations.idiomatic: I fell from the railing here once — I cannot help my sorrow.

sentences.zh: 邦曜即分嫁女資，擇士人歸之。

translations.literal: Bangyao immediately set aside bridal funds, chose a gentleman, and sent her away in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyao at once provided dowry funds, chose a scholar, and married her out honorably.

sentences.zh: 其篤於內行如此。

translations.literal: Such was his depth of domestic virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his devotion within the household.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保、左都御史，謚忠介。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and Left Censor-in-Chief; posthumous title Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and Left Censor-in-Chief with the title Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚忠湣。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty granted the posthumous title Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 淩義渠，字駿甫，烏程人。

translations.literal: Ling Yiqu, courtesy name Junfu, was a man of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Yiqu, courtesy name Junfu, was from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1625.

sentences.zh: 除行人。

translations.literal: Appointed Junior Commissioner in the Bureau of Foreign Tributaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Junior Commissioner in the Bureau of Foreign Tributaries.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年授禮科給事中，知無不言。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he was made supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites and spoke out on whatever he knew.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 3 he became a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites and spoke plainly on every issue he knew.

sentences.zh: 三河知縣劉夢煒失餉銀三千，責償急，自縊死，有司責其家。
