translations.literal: District Magistrate Liu Mengwei of Sanhe lost three thousand taels of ration silver; pressed hard to make restitution he hanged himself, and the authorities held his family liable.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhe magistrate Liu Mengwei lost three thousand taels of transport silver; driven to repay urgently he hanged himself, and officials demanded restitution from his family.

sentences.zh: 義渠言：「以金錢殞命吏，恐天下議朝廷重金，意不在盜也。」

translations.literal: Yiqu said: "That an official should lose his life over money — I fear the realm will think the court prizes gold above all, and that its heart is not on bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqu argued: "That an official should die over money will make the empire think the court values silver above all and cares nothing for thieves.

sentences.zh: 帝特原之。

translations.literal: The Emperor specially pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially exempted the family.

sentences.zh: 宜興、溧陽及遂安、壽昌民亂，焚掠巨室。

translations.literal: In Yixing, Liyang, Suian, and Shouchang the people rose in disorder, burning and plundering great houses.
translations.idiomatic: Uprisings in Yixing, Liyang, Suian, and Shouchang saw mobs burn and loot great houses.

sentences.zh: 義渠言：「魏羽林軍焚領軍張彜第，高歡以為天下事可知，日者告密漸啟，藩國悍宗入京越奏，裏閭小故叫閽聲冤，仆豎侮家長，下吏箝上官，市儈持縉紳，此《春秋》所謂六逆也。

translations.literal: Yiqu said: "When Wei guardsmen burned the residence of the commander Zhang Yi, Gao Huan took it as a sign that the world's affairs could be read; lately secret denunciations have gradually opened; fierce clansmen of the imperial house enter the capital to memorial beyond their rank; neighborhood trifles shout at the palace gates for redress; servants insult their masters; lower officials clamp their superiors; market folk hold gentry hostage — these are what the Spring and Autumn calls the six rebellions.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqu wrote: "When Wei guards burned Commander Zhang Yi's mansion, Gao Huan judged that one could read the fate of the realm; lately informers multiply; fierce collateral princes come to Beijing with irregular memorials; neighborhoods bring petty quarrels clamoring at the palace gates; servants insult their masters; junior officials muzzle their superiors; tradesmen lord it over the gentry — these are the Six Rebellions of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 天下所以治，恃上下之分。

translations.literal: The realm is governed by relying on the distinction between high and low.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is kept in order only by the distinction between high and low.

sentences.zh: 防維決裂，即九重安所藉以提挈萬靈哉！」

translations.literal: If defenses and bonds rupture, on what can the Ninefold Height rely to lead the myriad souls!
translations.idiomatic: Once those bonds crack, what can the throne lean on to govern all beneath Heaven!

sentences.zh: 義渠與溫體仁同里，無所附麗。

translations.literal: Yiqu was from the same district as Wen Tiren and attached to no faction.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqu and Wen Tiren were fellow townsmen; he joined no faction.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉含輝劾體仁擬旨失當，被貶二秩。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Liu Hanhui impeached Tiren for improper drafting of rescripts and was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Liu Hanhui impeached Wen Tiren for improper drafting of edicts and was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 義渠言：「諫官不得規執政失，而委申飭權於部院，反得制言路。

translations.literal: Yiqu said: "If remonstrators may not criticize the chief minister's faults, but hand enforcement authority to ministries and courts, they instead gain control of the remonstrance path.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqu argued: "When censors may not reprove the chief minister's errors yet surrender the power of rebuke to ministries, those ministries end up controlling the voice of criticism.

sentences.zh: 大臣以攬權為奉旨，小臣以結舌為盡職，將貽國家無窮憂。」

translations.literal: Great ministers take grasping power as serving the edict; petty officers take silence as fulfilling duty — they will bequeath unending worry to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers treat seizing power as obedience; junior officials treat silence as loyalty — the dynasty will inherit endless trouble.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書張鳳翼敘廢將陳狀猷功，為給事中劉昌所駁，昌反被斥。

translations.literal: War Minister Zhang Fengyi listed merits of dismissed generals and was impeached by Liu Chang; yet Chang was himself expelled.
translations.idiomatic: War Minister Zhang Fengyi recited the achievements of dismissed generals; supervising secretary Liu Chang refuted him — yet Liu Chang was the one dismissed.

sentences.zh: 義渠言：「今上下盡相蒙，疆埸欺蔽為甚。

translations.literal: Yiqu said: "Now high and low entirely deceive one another; on the borders concealment is worst.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqu wrote: "Today every level deceives the next; frontier falsification is worst of all.

sentences.zh: 官方盡濫徇，武弁幸功為甚。

translations.literal: Official posts are lavishly granted in self-interest; military officers fabricate merit above all.
translations.idiomatic: Civil posts are handed out with abandon; officers fake exploits more than anything.

sentences.zh: 中樞不職，舍其大，摘其細，已足為言者羞。

translations.literal: The central command fails in its duty; abandoning the great to pick at the small is already shame enough for remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: The central ministries neglect their charge; when even that is set aside to nitpick small matters, critics should be ashamed.

sentences.zh: 辨疏一入，調用隨之。

translations.literal: Once a rebuttal memorial enters, transfer and appointment follow.
translations.idiomatic: One rebuttal submitted, and the speaker is soon transferred.

sentences.zh: 自今奸弊叢生，功罪倒置，言者將杜口。」

translations.literal: From now corruption will cluster and merit and guilt invert; remonstrators will shut their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth abuses will multiply, rewards and punishments will stand on their heads, and critics will fall silent.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: Not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 三遷兵科都給事中。

translations.literal: Three promotions to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was three times promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 東江自毛文龍後，叛者接踵。

translations.literal: East of the river, after Mao Wenlong, rebels followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: After Mao Wenlong, rebellion on the eastern islands followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 義渠言：「東島孤懸海外，轉餉艱，向仰給朝鮮。

translations.literal: Yiqu said: "The eastern island hangs alone on the ocean; transport of supplies is hard; formerly it relied on Korea for food.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqu wrote: "The eastern island stands isolated at sea; supplying it is arduous; it once depended on Korea for grain.

sentences.zh: 今路阻絕不得食，內潰可慮。」

translations.literal: Now the route is blocked and they cannot be fed — internal collapse is to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Now the routes are cut off and they cannot be fed — internal collapse is a real danger.

sentences.zh: 居無何，眾果潰，挾帥求撫。

translations.literal: Before long the masses indeed collapsed; they seized their commander and sought pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the troops did collapse, seizing their commander to demand enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 義渠言：「請陽撫陰剿，同惡必相戕。」

translations.literal: Yiqu said: "Request overt pacification and covert extermination — fellow evildoers will surely turn on one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqu urged: "Offer pacification in name while destroying them in secret — the wicked will turn on one another.

sentences.zh: 及命新帥出海，義渠言：「殲渠散黨宜速，速則可圖功，遲則更生他釁。」

translations.literal: When orders went out for a new commander to put to sea, Yiqu said: "Wiping out the ringleaders and scattering the parties must be swift; swift, merit can be won; slow, fresh troubles will rise."
translations.idiomatic: When a new commander was ordered to sea, Yiqu said: "Break the leaders and scatter the bands at once — speed brings success; delay breeds new trouble."

sentences.zh: 後其語皆驗。

translations.literal: Later his words were all verified.
translations.idiomatic: In time everything he predicted came true.

sentences.zh: 義渠居諫垣九年，建白多。

translations.literal: Yiqu spent nine years in the remonstrance posts, with many proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqu served nine years as a remonstrating official and offered many reforms.

sentences.zh: 吏科給事中劉安行惡之，以年例出義渠福建參政。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Anxing hated him and, under the seniority rule, sent Yiqu out as Fujian Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Liu Anxing disliked him and used the rotation rule to post Yiqu to Fujian as Administrator.

sentences.zh: 尋遷按察使，轉山東右布政使，所至有清操。

translations.literal: Soon promoted Surveillance Commissioner, then Shandong Right Provincial Commissioner — wherever he went he had pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Surveillance Commissioner, then Right Provincial Commissioner of Shandong, winning repute for integrity everywhere.

sentences.zh: 召拜南京光祿寺卿，署應天尹事。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing, acting as Magistrate of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Nanjing Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments with acting duties as Yingtian magistrate.

sentences.zh: 十六年，入為大理卿。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he entered office as Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 16 he was made Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，賊犯都城，有旨召對。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year the bandits assaulted the capital, and an edict summoned him to audience.
translations.idiomatic: The following March, as rebels assaulted the capital, an imperial summons called him to audience.

sentences.zh: 趨赴長安門，旦不啟扉。

translations.literal: He hurried to Chang'an Gate, but at dawn the doors had not yet been opened.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried to Chang'an Gate, but at dawn the gates were still shut.

sentences.zh: 俄傳城陷，還。

translations.literal: Soon word came that the city had fallen, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long word came that the city had fallen, and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 已，得帝崩問。

translations.literal: Afterward he received news that the emperor had died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he learned that the emperor was dead.

sentences.zh: 負墻哀號，首觸柱，血被面。

translations.literal: Leaning against the wall he wailed in grief, striking his head against a pillar until blood covered his face.
translations.idiomatic: He leaned against the wall and wailed, striking his head against a pillar until his face was covered with blood.

sentences.zh: 門生勸無死，義渠厲聲曰：「爾當以道義相勖，何姑息為！」

translations.literal: His students urged him not to die; Yiqu said sharply: "You ought to encourage one another with righteousness and duty—why offer me indulgence!"
translations.idiomatic: His students urged him not to die. Yiqu said sharply, "You should encourage me with righteousness and duty—why urge me toward indulgence!"

sentences.zh: 揮使去。

translations.literal: He gestured for them to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He waved them off and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 據幾端坐，取生平所好書籍盡焚之，曰：「無使賊手汙也。」

translations.literal: He sat upright at his desk, took all the books he had loved through life and burned them, saying: "Let no bandit hands defile them."
translations.idiomatic: He sat upright at his desk and burned every book he had cherished in life, saying, "Let no rebel hands defile them."

sentences.zh: 旦日具緋衣拜闕，作書辭父。

translations.literal: At dawn he put on scarlet robes and bowed toward the palace, and wrote a letter taking leave of his father.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he dressed in scarlet robes and bowed toward the palace, then wrote a farewell letter to his father.

sentences.zh: 已，自系，奮身絕吭而死，年五十二。

translations.literal: Then he bound himself and, throwing his body forward, cut his throat and died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Then he bound himself, threw himself forward, and cut his throat. He was fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈刑部尚書，謚忠清。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made minister of justice and given the posthumous title Zhong Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of justice and given the posthumous title Zhong Qing, "Loyal and Pure."

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚忠介。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous title Zhong Jie.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty granted him the posthumous title Zhong Jie, "Loyal and Incorruptible."

sentences.zh: 贊曰：範景文、倪元璐等皆莊烈帝腹心大臣，所共圖社稷者，國亡與亡，正也。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Fan Jingwen, Ni Yuanlu, and the rest were trusted ministers in the inner circle of Emperor Zhuanglie, who together plotted for the altars of state; when the state perished they perished with it—this was right.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Fan Jingwen, Ni Yuanlu, and their fellows were the Chongzhen Emperor's most trusted ministers, men who had staked their lives on the dynasty. When the state fell, they fell with it—and that was as it should be.

sentences.zh: 當時壎顏屈節，僥幸以偷生者，多被刑掠以死，身名俱裂，貽詬無窮。

translations.literal: At that time those who preserved their complexions and bent their principles, who hoped by luck to cling to life, were for the most part tortured to death; body and name were both shattered, and shame without end was left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had bowed and scraped, bent their principles, and clung to life by luck were mostly tortured to death in the end—ruined in body and name, and shamed forever.

sentences.zh: 而景文等樹義烈於千秋，荷褒揚於興代，名與日月爭光。

translations.literal: But Jingwen and the others planted righteous heroism for a thousand ages, received praise in the rising dynasty, and their names vie with sun and moon in glory.
translations.idiomatic: But Jingwen and his companions planted deeds of righteous heroism for all time, were honored by the new dynasty, and left names that shine beside the sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 以彼潔此，其相去得失何如也。

translations.literal: Compare the defiled with the pure—how vast the distance between loss and gain!
translations.idiomatic: Compare the one path with the other, and how vast the difference between ruin and honor.
